text: A company's engineering department is conducting a month-long test on the scalability of an in-house-developed software that requires a cluster of 100 or more servers. Which of the following models is the best to use?

options.text: PaaS
SaaS
BaaS
IaaS

explanation: Infrastructure as a Service rents raw compute, storage, and networking on demand, so the team can spin up a cluster of 100+ servers for a month, run its own in-house software with full control of the operating system, and release the capacity afterward. PaaS provides a managed runtime for building apps rather than controllable servers, SaaS delivers finished applications, and BaaS supplies backend services for mobile/web apps, so none of them fit a temporary self-managed server cluster.

text: What are three characteristics of change set deployments? Choose 3 answers.

options.text: Change sets can deploy custom settings data.
Change sets can only be used between related organizations.
Deployment is done in a one-way, single transaction.
Sending a change set between two orgs requires a deployment connection.
Change sets can be used to transfer records.

explanation: Change sets only move metadata between related orgs (production and its sandboxes), require a deployment connection authorized in the target org before an outbound change set can be uploaded, and deploy one way in a single transaction that either fully succeeds or rolls back. They carry metadata only, so neither custom settings data nor other records can be transferred with them; use Data Loader or another data tool for that.

text: Universal Containers wants to ensure that all new leads created in the system have a valid email address. They have already created a validation rule to enforce this requirement, but want to add an additional layer of validation using automation. What would be the best solution for this requirement?

options.text: Submit a REST API Callout with a JSON payload and validate the fields on a third party system
Use a before-save trigger on the Lead object to validate the email address and display an error message if it is invalid
Use a custom Lightning Web Component to make a callout to validate the fields on a third party system.
Use an Approval Process to enforce the completion of a valid email address using an outbound message action.

explanation: A before-save Apex trigger on Lead runs before the record is committed, so it can apply extra validation logic (for example a stricter regex check) and call addError() to block the save with a message, layering automation on top of the existing validation rule. A REST callout or LWC callout to a third party adds external dependencies and isn't enforced on every save, and an Approval Process with an outbound message doesn't validate or block data entry.

text: Which statement should be used to allow some of the records in a list of records to be inserted if others fail to be inserted?

options.text: Database.insert(records, true)
insert records
insert(records, false)
Database.insert(records, false)

explanation: Database.insert(records, false) sets allOrNone to false, so valid records are inserted and failures are returned in the Database.SaveResult array instead of rolling back the whole list. Database.insert(records, true) and the plain insert records DML statement are all-or-none and throw an exception on the first failure, and insert(records, false) is not valid Apex syntax because the DML statement takes no options parameter.

text: A developer identifies three triggers on the Expense__c object that process before delete, before insert, and before update events, respectively. Which two techniques should the developer implement to follow trigger best practices? Choose 2 answers.

options.text: Unify all three triggers into a single trigger on Expense__c that includes all events.
Unify the before insert and before update triggers and use Flow for the delete action.
Create helper classes to execute the appropriate logic when a record is saved.
Maintain all three triggers on Expense__c, but move the Apex logic out of the trigger definitions.

explanation: Trigger best practice is one trigger per object handling all events, which keeps the execution order predictable, combined with handler/helper classes that hold the logic so it is testable and reusable. Keeping three triggers leaves the order of execution undefined even if logic moves out, and splitting delete logic into a Flow scatters the automation across tools without addressing the multiple-trigger problem.

text: Which statement generates a list of Leads and Contacts that have a field containing the phrase "ACME"?

options.text: List<SObject> searchList = [FIND '*ACME*' IN FIELDS RETURNING Contact, Lead];
List<List<SObject>> searchList = [SELECT Name, Id FROM Contact, Lead WHERE Name LIKE '%ACME%'];
List<List<SObject>> searchList = [FIND '*ACME*' IN ALL FIELDS RETURNING Contact, Lead];
List<SObject> searchList = [find 'acme' in all fields returning Contact, Lead];

explanation: SOSL searches text across multiple objects, and FIND '*ACME*' IN ALL FIELDS RETURNING Contact, Lead is valid syntax that returns a List<List<SObject>> with one inner list per object. IN FIELDS is not a valid search group, SOSL results cannot be assigned to a flat List<SObject>, and SOQL cannot query two objects in one FROM clause, so the other statements fail to compile.

text: A developer creates a Lightning Web Component that imports a method from an Apex class. When a Validate button is pressed, the method runs complex validations. In this scenario, which two files/classes perform the Controller role in an MVC-style architecture? Choose 2 answers.

options.text: HTML file
Apex class
JavaScript file
XML file

explanation: In LWC's MVC-style split, the HTML template is the View, while the JavaScript file handles user events like the Validate button click and the imported Apex class runs the server-side validation logic, so both act as controllers. The XML file is only configuration metadata (targets, exposure, API version) and plays no part in handling requests or business logic.

text: What are two use cases for executing Anonymous Apex code? Choose 2 answers

options.text: schedule an Apex class to run periodically
To delete 15,000 inactive Accounts in a single transaction after a deployment
To run a batch Apex class to update all Contacts
To add unit test code coverage to an org

explanation: Anonymous Apex is well suited to ad hoc administrative tasks such as scheduling a class with System.schedule() or starting a batch job with Database.executeBatch() to update all Contacts. Deleting 15,000 records in one synchronous transaction exceeds the 10,000 DML rows limit, and Anonymous Apex cannot add code coverage because coverage comes only from running test methods.

text: A developer created a Lightning Web Component called statusComponent to be inserted into the Account record page. Which two things should the developer do to make this component available? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Add <target>lightning__RecordPage</target> to statusComponent.js.
Add <target>lightning__RecordPage</target> to statusComponent.js-meta.xml.
Set <isExposed>true</isExposed> in statusComponent.js-meta.xml.
Add <masterLabel>Account</masterLabel> to statusComponent.js-meta.xml.

explanation: Lightning App Builder only lists a component when its statusComponent.js-meta.xml file sets <isExposed>true</isExposed> and declares a supported target such as <target>lightning__RecordPage</target> inside <targets>. Targets belong in the metadata configuration file, not the JavaScript file, and <masterLabel> only sets the display name; restricting to Account would use <objects> inside <targetConfig>.

text: A developer creates a batch Apex job to update a large number of records, and receives reports of the job timing out and not completing. What is the first step towards troubleshooting the issue?

options.text: Check the asynchronous job monitoring page to view the job status and logs.
Check the debug logs for the batch job.
Disable the batch job and recreate it with a smaller number of records.
Decrease the batch size to reduce the load on the system.

explanation: The first step is to check Setup > Apex Jobs (asynchronous job monitoring) to see the job's status, batches processed, failures, and error messages, which shows where and why it stops. Debug logs are useful later but need trace flags set up first and are not the starting point, while reducing batch size or recreating the job are fixes you shouldn't apply before diagnosing the cause.

text: What are two benefits of using declarative customizations over code? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Declarative customizations automatically update with each Salesforce release.
Declarative customizations automatically generate test classes.
Declarative customizations cannot generate run time errors
Declarative customizations generally require less maintenance

explanation: Declarative tools are maintained by Salesforce, so they are upgraded with each release, and they generally need less ongoing maintenance than custom code because there are no test classes or code dependencies to manage. Declarative features do not generate test classes, and they can still fail at run time, for example with Flow faults or governor limit errors.

text:
Given the following Anonymous Apex block: 
List<Case> casesToUpdate = new List<Case>();
for (Case thisCase : [SELECT Id, Status FROM Case LIMIT 50000]) {
    thisCase.Status = 'Working';
    casesToUpdate.add(thisCase);
}
try {
    Database.update(casesToUpdate, false);
} catch (Exception e) {
    System.debug(e.getMessage());
}
What should a developer consider for an environment that has over 10,000 Case records?

options.text: The transaction will succeed and changes will be committed.
The try-catch block will handle exceptions thrown by governor limits.
The transaction will fail due to exceeding the governor limit.
The try/catch block will handle any DML exceptions thrown.

explanation: The query returns more than 10,000 Cases, and updating them all exceeds the 10,000 DML rows per transaction limit, so a System.LimitException is thrown and the whole transaction fails. Governor limit exceptions cannot be caught by try/catch, and Database.update(casesToUpdate, false) only allows partial success for record-level errors, not limit violations, so nothing is committed.

text: Which three Salesforce resources can be accessed from a Lightning Web Component? Choose 3 answers

options.text: Static resources
All external libraries
SVG resources
Third-party web components
Content asset files

explanation: LWC can import Salesforce resources through scoped modules: static resources via @salesforce/resourceUrl, content asset files via @salesforce/contentAssetUrl, and SVG resources included in the component bundle or a static resource. Not every external library is usable, since libraries must be loaded as static resources and comply with Lightning Locker or Lightning Web Security, and third-party web components are not supported in the same way.

text:
A developer must create a CreditCardPayment class that provides an implementation of an existing virtual Payment class: 
public virtual class Payment {
    public virtual void makePayment(Decimal amount) { }
}
Which implementation is correct?

options.text: public class CreditCardPayment extends Payment { public virtual void makePayment(Decimal amount) { /* implementation */ } }
public class CreditCardPayment implements Payment { public virtual void makePayment(Decimal amount) { /* implementation */ } }
public class CreditCardPayment implements Payment { public override void makePayment(Decimal amount) { /* implementation */ } }
public class CreditCardPayment extends Payment { public override void makePayment(Decimal amount) { /* implementation */ } }

explanation: Payment is a virtual class, so a subclass uses extends Payment, and redefining its virtual method requires the override keyword: public override void makePayment(Decimal amount). The implements keyword is only for interfaces, and declaring the method virtual in the subclass without override causes a compile error because it would hide the parent method.

text: A developer is creating a Lightning Web Component to show a list of sales records. The Sales Representative user should be able to see the commission field on each record. The Sales Assistant user should be able to see all fields on the record except the commission field. How should this be enforced so that the component works for both users without showing any errors?

options.text: Use WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED in the SOQL that fetches data for the component.
Use Security.stripInaccessible() to remove fields inaccessible to the current user.
Use Lightning Locker Service to enforce sharing rules and field-level security.
Use Lightning Data Service to get the collection of sales records.

explanation: Security.stripInaccessible() removes fields the running user can't read from the query results without throwing an error, so Sales Representatives see the commission field while Sales Assistants get the records without it. WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED throws an exception when any queried field is inaccessible, which would break the component for assistants, and Locker Service is a client-side security layer that does not enforce sharing or FLS.

text:
The following Apex method is executed by a Lightning Web Component in an org with more than 2,000 Lead records: 
@AuraEnabled
public static void updateOrigin() {
    for (Lead thisLead : [SELECT Id, Origin__c FROM Lead]) {
        thisLead.LeadSource = thisLead.Origin__c;
        update thisLead;
    }
}
Which governor limit will most likely be exceeded first?

options.text: Total number of SOQL queries issued
Total number of DML statements issued
Total number of records processed as a result of DML statements

explanation: The update thisLead statement sits inside the loop, so each Lead uses one DML statement, and the 150 DML statements per transaction limit is hit at Lead 151, long before the 2,000 records finish. Only one SOQL query is issued, and roughly 2,000 updated rows stay well below the 10,000 DML rows limit; bulkifying into a list and calling one update fixes the problem.

text:
A developer is asked to write helper methods that create test data for unit tests. Consider this class: 
public class TestUtils {
    public static Account createAccount() {
        Account acct = new Account();
        return acct;
    }
    // other helper methods
}
What should be changed so that TestUtils is usable only by unit tests?

options.text: Add @isTest above the createAccount() method only.
Add @isTest above the TestUtils class declaration.
Change the TestUtils class from public to private.
Remove static from createAccount().

explanation: Annotating the class with @isTest makes TestUtils a test-only class: it does not count toward the org's code size limit and can be called only from test code, which is exactly what a test data factory needs. Putting @isTest on the method alone doesn't restrict the class, a top-level class can't be declared private, and removing static only changes how the method is called.

text: Universal Containers transitioned from Salesforce Classic to Lightning Experience. A business process requires selected Opportunity values to be sent via an HTTP REST callout to an external order management system when a user presses a custom button on the Opportunity record page. Which two approaches can implement this requirement? Choose 2 answers.

options.text: Create a custom Visualforce quick action that performs the HTTP REST callout and use it on the Opportunity record page.
Create an after-update trigger on Opportunity that calls a helper method using @future(callout=true).
Create a Lightning component quick action that performs the HTTP REST callout and use it on the Opportunity record page.
Create a Remote Action that performs the HTTP REST callout whenever Opportunity is updated.

explanation: A button on the Lightning record page can be a quick action backed by a Visualforce page or a Lightning component (Aura or LWC), and either can call an Apex method that performs the HTTP callout with the selected Opportunity values when the user clicks it. An after-update trigger or a Remote Action tied to every update fires on any save rather than on the user's button press, so neither meets the requirement.

text: A developer has an integer variable called maxAttempts. The developer needs to ensure that once maxAttempts is initialized, it preserves its value for the length of the Apex transaction; while being able to share the variable's state between trigger executions. How should the developer declare maxAttempts to meet these requirements?

options.text: Declare maxAttempts as a constant using the static and final keywords.
Declare maxAttempts as a member variable on the trigger definition.
Declare maxAttempts as an instance variable on a helper class.
Declare maxAttempts as a private static variable on a helper class.

explanation: A static variable on a helper class is initialized once per transaction and keeps its value across every trigger execution in that transaction, so it can share state between trigger invocations; making it private wraps it in the class. A static final constant can't hold state that changes, triggers can't declare usable member variables that persist, and an instance variable resets each time a new helper object is created.

text: A developer deployed a trigger to update the status__c of Assets related to an Account when the Account's status changes and a nightly integration that updates Accounts in bulk has started to fail with limit failures. What should the developer change about the code to address the failure while still having the code update all of the Assets correctly?

options.text: Move all of the logic to a Queueable class that queries for and updates the Assets and call it from the trigger.
Add List<Asset> assets = [SELECT Id, Status__c FROM Asset WHERE AccountId = :acctId] inside the existing per-Account helper and iterate over that list.
Add a LIMIT clause to the SOQL query on line 16 to limit the number of Assets queried for an Account.
Change the getAssetsToUpdate method to process all Accounts in one call and call it outside of the for loop that starts on line 03.

explanation: Exam key: the limit failures come from calling the Asset helper once per Account inside the loop, so it runs one query per Account; changing getAssetsToUpdate to accept all Accounts and calling it once outside the loop that starts on line 03 bulkifies the query. Moving the same logic to Queueable doesn't fix the per-Account query pattern, adding a query inside the per-Account helper makes it worse, and a LIMIT would skip Assets. Note: the trigger code the question refers to (lines 03 and 16) is not included in the source.
reviewNote: Key taken from the source; the referenced trigger code exhibit (lines 03 and 16) is missing.

text: Universal Containers (UC) wants to lower its shipping cost while making the shipping process more efficient. The Distribution Officer advises UC to implement global addresses to allow multiple Accounts to share a default pickup address. The developer is tasked to create the supporting object and relationship for this business requirement and uses the Setup Menu to create a custom object called "Global Address". Which field should the developer add to create the most efficient model that supports the business need?

options.text: Add a master-detail field on the Global Address object to the Account object.
Add a lookup field on the Global Address object to the Account object.
Add a lookup field on the Account object to the Global Address object.
Add a master-detail field on the Account object to the Global Address object.

explanation: Many Accounts share one Global Address, so Global Address is the parent and each Account needs a lookup field pointing to it. A lookup on Global Address to Account would let each address link to only one Account, and a master-detail field on Account to Global Address would force every Account to have an address and inherit its sharing and ownership, which is too restrictive for a standard object like Account.

text: Universal Containers uses standard order management with a master-detail relationship between Order and Order Line Item. Each Order Line Item stores an availability date, and an Order can ship only when all line items are available. Which method should be used to calculate the estimated ship date for an Order?

options.text: Use a LATEST formula on each of the latest availability date fields.
Use a CEILING formula on each of the latest availability date fields.
Use a DAYS formula on each of the availability date fields and a COUNT Roll-Up Summary field on the Order.
Use a MAX Roll-Up Summary field on the latest availability date fields.

explanation: Because Order and Order Line Item have a master-detail relationship, a Roll-Up Summary field on Order using MAX over the line items' availability date returns the latest date, which is when every item is available and the Order can ship. Formula fields cannot aggregate across child records, and LATEST is not a Salesforce formula function, CEILING rounds numbers, and a COUNT roll-up only counts line items.

text: Universal Containers has an order system that uses an Order Number to identify an order for customers and service agents. Order records will be imported into Salesforce. How should the Order Number field be defined in Salesforce?

options.text: Indirect Lookup
Direct Lookup
External ID and Unique
Lookup

explanation: Marking the Order Number as an External ID with the Unique attribute indexes it and guarantees no duplicates, and it lets imports and upserts match existing Salesforce records using the external system's identifier. Lookup, Direct Lookup, and Indirect Lookup are relationship field types (the latter two used with external objects), not ways to store and match a unique identifier on imported records.

text: In terms of the MVC paradigm, what are two advantages of implementing the view layer of a Salesforce application using Lightning Web Component-based development over Visualforce? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Rich component ecosystem
Leg capturing via the Debug Logs Setup page
Built-in standard and custom set controllers
Self-contained and reusable units of an application

explanation: LWC view development benefits from a rich ecosystem of base Lightning components and AppExchange components, and from building self-contained, reusable components that can be combined across pages and apps. Log capture through the Debug Logs Setup page is a platform feature unrelated to the view technology, and built-in standard and set controllers are actually a Visualforce feature, not an LWC advantage.

text: What are two ways a developer can get the status of an enqueued job for a class that implements the queueable interface? Choose 2 answers

options.text: View the Apex Status page
View the Apex Jobs page
Query the AsyncApexJob object
View the Apex Flex Queue

explanation: Each queued job is recorded as an AsyncApexJob record, so you can query it with the job ID returned by System.enqueueJob(), or view the same information on Setup > Apex Jobs. There is no Apex Status page, and the Apex Flex Queue only holds batch jobs waiting to be processed, not Queueable jobs.

text: Which statement describes the execution order when multiple triggers are associated with the same object and event?

options.text: Triggers are executed in the order they are modified.
Trigger execution order cannot be guaranteed.
Triggers are executed alphabetically by trigger name.
Triggers are executed in the order they are created.

explanation: Salesforce does not guarantee the order in which multiple triggers on the same object and event run, regardless of their names, creation dates, or modification dates. This is why best practice is a single trigger per object that passes control to a handler class, so the developer controls the order explicitly.

text: A developer created a child Lightning Web Component nested inside a parent Lightning Web Component. The parent needs to pass a string value to the child. In which two ways can this be accomplished? Choose 2 answers

options.text: The parent component can invoke a public method in the child component.
The parent component can use a public property to pass the data to the child component
The parent can use the Apex controller class to send data to the child component.
The parent component can use a custom event to pass the data to the child component.

explanation: A parent passes data down to a child by setting a public property decorated with @api in the child's markup, or by calling a public @api method on the child through this.template.querySelector(). Custom events flow upward from child to parent, not downward, and an Apex controller doesn't pass values between components on the client.

text:
Given this Apex code: 
Boolean isOK;
Integer x;
String theString = 'Hello';
if (isOK == false && theString == 'Hello') {
    x = 1;
} else if (isOK == true && theString == 'Hello') {
    x = 2;
} else if (isOK != null && theString == 'Hello') {
    x = 3;
} else {
    x = 4;
}
What is the value of x?
explanation: isOK is declared but never initialized, so its value is null. Comparing null == false and null == true both return false, and isOK != null is also false, so none of the if/else if branches match and execution falls through to the final else, setting x to 4.

text: A developer completed a feature consisting of an Apex trigger and a trigger-handler Apex class. Which two factors must be considered to deploy them properly to production? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Apex classes must have at least 75% code coverage org-wide.
All methods in the test classes must use @istest.
At least one line of code must be executed for the trigger.
Test methods must be declared with the testMethod keyword.

explanation: Deploying Apex to production requires the tests to cover at least 75% of Apex code overall, and each trigger must have some coverage, meaning at least one line must execute during tests. Test methods only need @isTest (the testMethod keyword is deprecated, not required), and helper methods in a test class don't all have to be annotated.

text: How does the Lightning Component framework help developers implement solutions faster?

options.text: By providing device-awareness for mobile and desktops
By providing an Agile process with default steps
By providing change history and version control
By providing code review standards and processes

explanation: The Lightning Component framework provides ready-made, responsive building blocks that adapt to mobile and desktop devices, so developers don't have to code separate device-specific experiences. Agile processes, change history and version control, and code review standards come from development methodology and external tools, not from the component framework.

text: A developer wants to send an outbound message when a record meets specific criteria. Which two features satisfy this use case? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Flow Builder can be used to check the record criteria and send an outbound message.
Approval Process can be used to check the record criteria and send an outbound message without Apex code.
Entitlement Process can be used to check the record criteria and send an outbound message without Apex code.
Next Best Action can be used to check the record criteria and send an outbound message.

explanation: Outbound messages can be sent without Apex from an Approval Process, as an approval, rejection, or recall action, and from Flow Builder, which can test criteria in a record-triggered flow and use the Outbound Message action. Entitlement Processes trigger milestone actions such as tasks, email alerts, and field updates but don't send outbound messages, and Next Best Action shows recommendations to users rather than sending messages automatically.

text: Universal Containers hires a developer to build a custom search page to help users find the Accounts they want. Users will be able to search on Name, Description, and a custom comments field. Which consideration should the developer be aware of when deciding between SOQL and SOSL? Choose 2 answers

options.text: SOSL is faster for text searches.
SOQL is able to return more records
SOQL is faster for text searches.
SOSL is able to return more records.

explanation: SOSL uses the search index, so it is faster for text searches across fields like Name, Description, and long comments, while SOQL LIKE filters on text are slower and can't filter long text areas well. SOQL can return up to 50,000 records per transaction, while a SOSL query returns at most 2,000 results, so SOQL returns more records.

text: What is an example of a polymorphic lookup field in Salesforce?

options.text: The ParentId field on the standard Account object
A custom field, Link__c, on the standard Contact object that looks up to an Account or a Campaign
The WhatId field on the standard Event object
The LeadId and ContactId fields on the standard Campaign Member object

explanation: The WhatId field on Event (and Task) is polymorphic: a single lookup can point to different object types such as Account, Opportunity, Campaign, or custom objects. ParentId on Account always refers to another Account, a custom lookup can target only one object, and Campaign Member's LeadId and ContactId are two separate single-object lookups.

text: A developer has a Visualforce page and custom controller to save Account records. The developer wants to display any validation rule violations to the user. How can the developer make sure that validation rule violations are displayed?

options.text: Add custom controller attributes to display the message.
Use a try/catch with a custom exception class.
Include <apex:messages> on the Visualforce page.
Perform the DML using Database.upsert().

explanation: When a DML statement in the controller fails a validation rule, the error is added to the page's message collection, and an <apex:messages> (or <apex:pageMessages>) component renders these messages to the user. Custom attributes or custom exceptions add work without automatically showing the validation error, and Database.upsert() only changes how the DML is performed.

text: Which code displays the contents of a Visualforce page as a PDF?

options.text: <apex:page renderAs="application/pdf">
<apex:page renderAs="pdf">
<apex:page contentType="application/pdf">
<apex:page contentType="pdf">

explanation: Visualforce invokes its PDF rendering service when the page sets renderAs="pdf" on <apex:page>. renderAs only accepts pdf (not a MIME type like application/pdf), and contentType only sets the HTTP response header, so it doesn't convert the page into a PDF.

text: Universal Containers wants Opportunities to no longer be editable when they reach the Closed/Won stage. Which two strategies can a developer use to accomplish this? Choose 2 answers.

options.text: Use an automatically launched Approval Process.
Use a Validation Rule.
Use a before-save Trigger.
Use an Auto-Response Rule.

explanation: Exam key: a validation rule such as AND(NOT(ISNEW()), ISPICKVAL(PRIORVALUE(StageName), 'Closed Won')) blocks any later edit, and an Approval Process locks the record so only admins or approvers can edit it. Auto-Response Rules only send emails for leads and cases. Note: approval processes aren't launched automatically on their own (they need a submit step, for example from a Flow), and a before-save trigger calling addError() also prevents edits, so the trigger is arguably a more correct second answer than the Approval Process.
reviewNote: Key questionable: a before-save trigger with addError() reliably prevents edits, while approval processes require submission and are not automatically launched.

text: While writing an Apex class, a developer wants to make sure that all functionality being developed is handled as specified by the requirements. Which approach should the developer use to be sure that the Apex class is working according to specifications?

options.text: Include a savepoint and Database.rollback().
Include a try/catch block to the Apex class.
Run the code in an Execute Anonymous block in the Developer Console.
Create a test class to execute the business logic and run the test in the Developer Console.

explanation: A test class with test methods that run the business logic and check the results with System.assert methods verifies the class against its requirements, and running it in the Developer Console shows pass/fail results and coverage. Savepoints and try/catch blocks handle errors and transactions but don't verify behavior, and a one-off Execute Anonymous run proves nothing repeatable.

text: Which code in a Visualforce page and/or controller might present a security vulnerability?

options.text: <apex:outputText value="{!$CurrentPage.parameters.userInput}" />
<apex:outputText escape="false" value="{!$CurrentPage.parameters.userInput}" />
<apex:outputField value="{!ctrl.userInput}" rendered="{!isEditable}" />
<apex:outputField value="{!ctrl.userInput}" />

explanation: Setting escape="false" on <apex:outputText> outputs the URL parameter userInput as raw HTML, so an attacker can inject script in the query string, which is a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. By default <apex:outputText> and <apex:outputField> escape their output, so the other snippets render user input safely.

text: What should a developer use to script the deployment and unit test execution as part of continuous integration?

options.text: VS Code
Execute Anonymous
Salesforce CLI
Developer Console

explanation: Salesforce CLI (sf) commands can be scripted in a CI pipeline to authenticate, deploy metadata, and run Apex tests with results returned as machine-readable output. VS Code is an interactive editor, and Execute Anonymous and the Developer Console are manual browser-based tools, so none of them can be scripted into an automated pipeline.

text: The Job_Application__c custom object has a field that is a master-detail relationship to the Contact object, where the Contact object is the master. As part of a feature implementation, a developer needs to retrieve a list containing all Contact records where the related Account Industry is 'Technology', while also retrieving the Contact's Job_Application__c records. Based on the object's relationships, what is the most efficient statement to retrieve the list of Contacts?

options.text: [SELECT Id, (SELECT Id FROM Job_Applications__r) FROM Contact WHERE Accounts.Industry = 'Technology']
[SELECT Id, (SELECT Id FROM Job_Application__c) FROM Contact WHERE Accounts.Industry = 'Technology']
[SELECT Id, (SELECT Id FROM Job_Application__c) FROM Contact WHERE Account.Industry = 'Technology']
[SELECT Id, (SELECT Id FROM Job_Applications__r) FROM Contact WHERE Account.Industry = 'Technology']

explanation: The parent-to-parent path from Contact to Account uses the relationship name Account, so the filter is Account.Industry = 'Technology', and the child subquery uses the plural relationship name Job_Applications__r rather than the object API name. Accounts.Industry is not a valid relationship, and FROM Job_Application__c in a subquery fails because subqueries must use the child relationship name.

text: Universal Containers (UC) processes orders in Salesforce in a custom object, Order__c. They also allow sales reps to upload CSV files with thousands of orders at a time. A Queueable started from the trigger when the status first becomes 'Placed' supports callouts. It can process the orders one at a time and chain further jobs to handle large CSV loads without hitting @future limits. Plain @future calls run out quickly when thousands of rows arrive at once, since each trigger chunk enqueues one. A scheduled batch adds delay, and a flow action still runs inside the trigger transaction.

text: A developer created an Apex trigger that calls MyClass.myStaticMethod(). Developer Console

explanation: The Developer Console's Query Plan tool shows the cost, cardinality, and index use of SOQL queries. Its debug logs, timeline, and Performance Tree help pinpoint slow queries when a page loads. Setup menu pages and AppExchange don't provide query profiling. VS Code with the Salesforce Extensions is an editor and lacks the Console's built-in Query Plan view.

text: A company has a custom object, Order__c, with a required unique External ID field called Order_Number__c. Which statement performs the DML needed to insert new records and update existing records in a List<Order__c> by matching on that External ID?

options.text: merge orders;
merge orders Order_Number__c;
upsert orders Order_Number__c;
upsert orders;

explanation: upsert orders Order_Number__c; matches each record on the external ID field. It updates records whose value already exists and inserts the rest in a single DML statement. A bare upsert orders; matches on the record Id, which new records don't have, so existing orders would be duplicated. merge combines up to three records of the same type into one and can't insert new records.

text: An org has an existing flow that edits an Opportunity with an Update Records element. A developer must update the flow to also create a Contact and store the created Contact's ID on the Opportunity. Which update must the developer make in the flow?

options.text: Add a new Update Records element.
Add a new Roll Back Records element.
Add a new Create Records element.
Add a new Get Records element.

explanation: The flow needs a Create Records element to insert the Contact. Its option to store the new record's Id in a variable then makes the Id available to the existing Update Records element for the Opportunity. Another Update Records element can't create a record, and Get Records only queries existing data. Roll Back Records undoes pending changes rather than adding data.

text: Which Lightning Web Component custom event property settings enable the event to bubble up the containment hierarchy and cross the Shadow DOM boundary?

options.text: bubbles: true, composed: false
bubbles: false, composed: false
bubbles: true, composed: true
bubbles: false, composed: true

explanation: bubbles: true makes the event travel up through the component's ancestors. composed: true lets it cross the shadow DOM boundary into the containing components' trees. Both are needed for the event to reach handlers outside the component's own shadow tree. With composed: false the event stops at the shadow root. With bubbles: false the event doesn't travel up through ancestors.

text: Universal Containers needs to create a custom user interface component that allows users to enter information about their accounts. The component should be able to validate the user input before saving the information to the database. What is the best technology to create this component?

options.text: Flow
Lightning Web Components
Visualforce
VUE JavaScript framework

explanation: Lightning Web Components are the recommended technology for custom Salesforce UI. They provide client-side validation through base components such as lightning-input, reportValidity(), and custom validity messages before Apex or Lightning Data Service saves the data. Flow is declarative and limited for custom UI, and Visualforce is legacy technology. Vue isn't a Salesforce-native framework for components on Lightning pages.

text: How should a developer write unit tests for a private method in an Apex class?

options.text: Use the SeeAllData annotation.
Add a test method in the Apex class.
Mark the Apex class as global.
Use the @TestVisible annotation.

explanation: Annotating a private method or variable with @TestVisible lets test classes access it without changing its access modifier. SeeAllData controls access to org data, not method visibility. Since API 28.0, test methods can't be placed in non-test classes. Making the class global exposes it outside the namespace, which doesn't grant access to private members.

text: Assuming name is a String obtained from a Visualforce page, which two SOQL approaches are safe from SOQL injection? Choose 2 answers

options.text: String query = '%' + name + '%'; List<Account> results = [SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Name LIKE :query];
String query = 'SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Name LIKE \'%' + name + '%\''; List<Account> results = Database.query(query);
String query = 'SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Name LIKE \'%' + String.escapeSingleQuotes(name) + '%\''; List<Account> results = Database.query(query);
String query = 'SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Name LIKE \'%' + name + '%\''; List<Account> results = Database.query(query);

explanation: A static SOQL query with a bind variable (:query) treats user input strictly as data, so it can't change the query structure. Dynamic SOQL is safe when the input is passed through String.escapeSingleQuotes(), which escapes quotes an attacker could use to break out of the string literal. Concatenating the raw name into a Database.query() string leaves the query open to injection.

text: Universal Containers has implemented an order management application. Each Order can have one or more Order Line items. The Order Line object is related to the Order via a master-detail relationship. For each Order Line item, the total price is calculated by multiplying the Order Line item price with the quantity ordered. What is the best practice to get the sum of all Order Line item totals on the Order record?

options.text: Roll-up summary field
Formula field
trigger
Quick action

explanation: Because Order Line is the detail side of a master-detail relationship, a roll-up summary field on Order can SUM the line total field. The platform keeps the sum up to date automatically, with no code. A formula field can't aggregate values from child records. A trigger could do it but adds code to maintain when a declarative feature already exists. A quick action doesn't calculate stored totals.

text: While developing an Apex class with custom search functionality that will be launched from a Lightning Web Component, how can the developer ensure only records accessible to the currently logged in user are displayed?

options.text: Use the WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED clause within the SOQL.
Use the inherited sharing keyword.
Use the with sharing keyword.
Use the without sharing keyword.

explanation: Declaring the class with sharing makes its SOQL and SOSL respect the running user's sharing rules, so the search returns only records the user can see. inherited sharing takes the caller's mode. That is safe from an LWC but less explicit, and the exam expects with sharing. without sharing ignores sharing. WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED checks object and field permissions, not record-level access.

text: What can be easily developed using the Lightning Component framework?

options.text: Salesforce Classic user interface pages
Lightning Pages
Customized JavaScript buttons
Salesforce integrations

explanation: The Lightning Component framework (Aura and LWC) is used to build components that are assembled into Lightning Pages in Lightning App Builder, such as record, home, and app pages. Classic UI pages are built with Visualforce. JavaScript buttons are a Classic-only feature that Lightning doesn't support. Integrations are built with APIs and Apex rather than the UI component framework.

text: While working in a sandbox, an Apex test fails when run in the Test Runner. However, executing the Apex logic in the Execute Anonymous window succeeds with no exceptions or errors. Why did the method fail in the sandbox test framework but succeed in the Developer Console?

options.text: The test method does not use System.runAs() to execute as a specific user.
The test method is calling an @future method.
The test method relies on existing data in the sandbox.
The test method has a syntax error in the code.

explanation: By default, Apex tests can't see existing org data (SeeAllData=false). Logic that works in Execute Anonymous, which runs against real sandbox records, can fail in a test that expects those records to exist. A syntax error would stop the code from compiling or saving at all. A missing System.runAs() or an @future call doesn't by itself cause a pass in one place and a failure in the other.

text:
How many Accounts are committed by the following Apex block? 
for (Integer i = 0; i < 500; i++) {
    Account a = new Account(Name = 'New Account ' + i);
    insert a;
}
explanation: Each loop pass runs a separate insert, and a synchronous transaction allows only 150 DML statements. The 151st insert throws a System.LimitException, which can't be caught. That rolls back the whole transaction, so no Accounts are committed. The answer isn't 150, because the first 150 inserts aren't saved separately. All 500 would only succeed if the records were collected into a list and inserted once.

text: Which two characteristics are true for Lightning Web Component custom events? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Data may be passed in the payload of a custom event using @wire decorated properties.
Data may be passed in the payload of a custom event using a property called detail.
By default a custom event only propagates to its immediate container and to its immediate child component.
By default a custom event only propagates to its immediate container.

explanation: A CustomEvent carries its payload in the detail property, for example new CustomEvent('select', { detail: recordId }). By default bubbles and composed are false, so only the immediate container that listens on the child component receives the event. Events never travel down to child components. @wire properties provision data from a wire adapter and aren't used to build an event payload.

text: Cloud Kicks has a multi-screen flow that its call center agents use when handling inbound service desk calls. At one of the steps in the flow, the agents should be presented with a list of order numbers and dates that are retrieved from an external order management system in real time and displayed on the screen. What should a developer use to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: An outbound message
An Apex REST class
An Apex controller
An invocable method

explanation: Screen flows call Apex through an @InvocableMethod. That method can make the real-time callout to the order management system and return the order numbers and dates for a screen to display. An Apex REST class exposes Salesforce to inbound callers rather than calling out. Outbound messages are one-way, workflow-driven SOAP notifications that return no data. A plain Apex controller backs Visualforce or Lightning components, and Flow can't call it.

text: Where are two locations a developer can look to find information about the status of batch or future methods? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Developer Console
Apex Jobs
Paused Flow Interviews component
Apex Flex Queue

explanation: The Apex Jobs page in Setup lists the status, submitted date, and errors for batch, future, queueable, and scheduled jobs. The Developer Console also lets you check asynchronous execution through its logs and query AsyncApexJob. The Apex Flex Queue shows only batch jobs waiting in Holding status, not future methods. Paused Flow Interviews relate to flows, not Apex.

text: A lead developer creates a virtual class called OrderRequest. Given a CustomerOrder class, how can a developer use OrderRequest as its parent class?

options.text: public class CustomerOrder extends(class="OrderRequest") { }
public class CustomerOrder implements OrderRequest { }
public class CustomerOrder extends OrderRequest { }
@Implements(class="OrderRequest") public class CustomerOrder { }

explanation: In Apex, inheritance from a virtual or abstract class uses the extends keyword: public class CustomerOrder extends OrderRequest { }. implements is only for interfaces. There is no extends(class=...) syntax and no @Implements annotation in Apex.

text: What is the value of the Trigger.old context variable in a before insert trigger?

options.text: An empty list of sObjects
Undefined
null
A list of newly created sObjects without IDs

explanation: Trigger.old holds the previous versions of records and is only available in update and delete triggers. In an insert trigger no prior version exists, so Trigger.old is null rather than an empty list. The newly created records without Ids are in Trigger.new. Apex has no "undefined" value.

text:
Given the following Apex method: 
public static void updateAccounts(List<Account> theseAccounts) {
    for (Account thisAccount : theseAccounts) {
        if (thisAccount.Website == null) {
            thisAccount.Website = 'https://www.demo.com';
        }
    }
    update theseAccounts;
}
When the DML operation throws a DmlException, how should the developer modify the code to handle the exception gracefully?

options.text: Replace update with upsert.
Implement Change Data Capture.
Wrap the DML operation in a try/catch block for DmlException.
Remove null items from the Account list.

explanation: Wrapping the update in try { ... } catch (DmlException e) { ... } lets the method catch the failure, log it or report it to the user, and continue instead of throwing an unhandled exception. Switching to upsert doesn't stop DML exceptions. Change Data Capture publishes change events and isn't error handling. Removing null items avoids one possible cause but doesn't handle other DML failures such as validation errors.

text: A developer wants to import 500 Opportunity records into a sandbox. Why should the developer choose to use Data Loader instead of Data Import Wizard?

options.text: Data Loader automatically relates Opportunities to Accounts.
Data Loader runs from the developer's browser.
Data Import Wizard does not support Opportunities.
Data Import Wizard cannot import all 500 records

explanation: Data Import Wizard supports Accounts, Contacts, Leads, Solutions, Campaign Members, Person Accounts, and custom objects, but not Opportunities. Data Loader is required for this import. 500 records is well within the wizard's 50,000-record limit, so volume isn't the reason. Data Loader is a desktop client, not a browser tool. Opportunities are linked to Accounts by supplying AccountId values, not automatically.

text: A Next Best Action strategy uses an Enhance Element that invokes an Apex method to determine a discount level for a Contact, based on a number of factors. What is the correct definition of the Apex method?

options.text: @InvocableMethod global static List<List<Recommendation>> getLevel(List<ContactWrapper> input) { /*implementation*/ }
@InvocableMethod global Recommendation getLevel(ContactWrapper input) { /*implementation*/ }
@InvocableMethod global List<List<Recommendation>> getLevel(List<ContactWrapper> input) { /*implementation*/ }
@InvocableMethod global static List<Recommendation> getLevel(List<ContactWrapper> input) { /*implementation*/ }

explanation: Exam key: the method must be a global static @InvocableMethod that takes a bulk List input and returns a List<Recommendation>. Non-static methods and single-object signatures are invalid for invocable actions. Note: the Next Best Action documentation says an Apex action used in a Generate or Enhance element returns List<List<Recommendation>>, one inner list per request, which matches the static List<List<Recommendation>> option. An Enhance method also normally receives the incoming recommendations as input.
reviewNote: Key appears incorrect: NBA documentation shows Enhance/Generate invocable methods returning List<List<Recommendation>> (the static option).

text: Universal Containers decided to transition from Classic to Lightning Experience. They asked a developer to replace a JavaScript button that was being used to create records with prepopulated values. What can the developer use to accomplish this?

options.text: Validation rules
triggers
Record triggered flows
Quick Actions

explanation: A Create a Record quick action with predefined field values opens a pre-filled form for the user. It is the Lightning-supported replacement for Classic JavaScript buttons that opened prepopulated create pages. Validation rules only block bad data. Triggers and record-triggered flows run after a save and don't give the user a pre-filled form to start from.

text: Universal Containers has developed custom Apex code and Lightning Components in a Sandbox environment. They need to deploy the code and associated configurations to the Production environment. What is the recommended process for deploying the code and configurations to Production?

options.text: Use the Force.com IDE to deploy the Apex code and Lightning Components.
Use the Ant Migration Tool to deploy the Apex code and Lightning Components.
Use a change set to deploy the Apex code and Lightning Components.
Use Salesforce CLI to deploy the Apex code and Lightning Components.

explanation: Change sets are the native, point-and-click way to move Apex classes, Lightning components, and related configuration from a connected sandbox to production, and the deployment runs the required tests automatically. The Force.com IDE is retired, and the Ant Migration Tool and Salesforce CLI are script-driven Metadata API tools that work but are not the answer this question expects for a straightforward sandbox-to-production move. Note that for source-driven teams Salesforce now steers toward the CLI, so read this as the classic exam answer.

text: What are two considerations for deploying from a sandbox to production? Choose 2 answers

options.text: At least 75% of Apex code must be covered by unit tests.
Unit tests must have calls to the System.assert method.
Should deploy during business hours to ensure feedback can be quickly addressed.
All triggers must have at least one line of test coverage.

explanation: To deploy Apex to production, at least 75% of your Apex code must be covered by unit tests, and every trigger must have some test coverage (at least one covered line). Calling System.assert is a best practice, but the platform does not require it. Deploying during business hours is not a requirement either; deployments usually go out during low-usage windows so users aren't disrupted.

text: Universal Containers has a Visualforce page that displays a table of every Container__c being rented by a given Account. Recently this page is failing with a view state limit because some of the customers rent over 10,000 containers. What should a developer change about the Visualforce page to help with the page load errors?

options.text: Implement pagination with an OffsetController.
Implement pagination with a StandardSetController.
Use JavaScript remoting with SOQL Offset.
Use lazy loading and a transient List variable.

explanation: A StandardSetController paginates large record sets on the server, so only the current page of records goes into view state, which avoids the view state limit with 10,000+ containers. There is no standard OffsetController. SOQL OFFSET stops at 2,000 rows, so JavaScript remoting with OFFSET can't reach every record. A transient list keeps the data out of view state, but the page would still try to render every row at once.

text: Universal Containers decides to use purely declarative development to build out a new Salesforce application. Which two options can be used to build out the business logic layer for this application? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Record-Triggered Flow
Batch Jobs
Remote Actions
Validation Rules

explanation: Record-triggered flows and validation rules are both declarative tools for business logic: flows automate actions when records change, and validation rules enforce data rules when records are saved. Batch jobs (Database.Batchable) and Remote Actions (@RemoteAction) both need Apex code, so a purely declarative build can't use them.

text: A custom object Trainer__c has a lookup field to another custom object Gym__c. Which SOQL query will get the record for the Viridian City Gym and all its trainers?

options.text: SELECT Id FROM Trainer__c WHERE Gym__r.Name = 'Viridian City Gym'
SELECT Id, (SELECT Id FROM Trainer__c) FROM Gym__c WHERE Name = 'Viridian City Gym'
SELECT Id, (SELECT Id FROM Trainers__r) FROM Gym__c WHERE Name = 'Viridian City Gym'
SELECT Id, (SELECT Id FROM Trainers__c) FROM Gym__c WHERE Name = 'Viridian City Gym'

explanation: To get a parent record and its children in one query, you write a subquery on the child relationship name, which for a custom lookup ends in __r (here Trainers__r). The query starting from Trainer__c returns trainers, not the gym record. Subqueries that use the object API name Trainer__c, or Trainers__c with a __c suffix, are invalid relationship names.

text: Which three resources in an Aura component can contain JavaScript functions? Choose 3 answers

options.text: Style
Renderer
Controller
Design
Helper

explanation: An Aura component bundle holds JavaScript in three resources: the controller (action handlers), the helper (shared, reusable functions), and the renderer (custom rendering lifecycle overrides). The style resource is CSS, and the design resource is XML that exposes attributes to Lightning App Builder. Neither one contains JavaScript functions.

text: A developer created a custom order management app that uses an Apex class. The order is represented by an Order object and an OrderItem object that has a master-detail relationship to Order. During order processing, an order may be split into multiple orders. What should a developer do to allow the code to move existing OrderItem records to a new Order record?

options.text: Add without sharing to the Apex class declaration.
Change the master-detail relationship to an external lookup relationship.
Create a junction object between OrderItem and Order.
Select the Allow reparenting option on the master-detail relationship.

explanation: By default, a detail record in a master-detail relationship cannot be moved to a different master. Turning on Allow reparenting on the relationship field lets code change an OrderItem's parent to the new Order. without sharing only affects record visibility, not relationship rules. External lookups are for external objects. A junction object would build a many-to-many model and wouldn't solve the reparenting need.

text: What does the Lightning Component framework provide to developers?

options.text: Support for Classic and Lightning UIs
Prebuilt components that can be reused
Templates to create custom components
Extended governor limits for applications

explanation: The Lightning Component framework ships a library of prebuilt, reusable base components, such as buttons, inputs, and data tables, so developers can assemble apps quickly. It does not include templates for creating components, and it doesn't raise governor limits. Lightning components are built for Lightning Experience and the mobile app, not as a feature that provides Classic UI support.

text: An Opportunity needs to have an amount rolled up from a custom object that is not in a master-detail relationship. How can this be achieved?

options.text: Write a trigger on the Opportunity object and use tree sorting to sum the amount for all related child objects under the Opportunity.
Use the Streaming API to create real-time roll-up summaries.
Write a trigger on the child object and use an aggregate function to sum the amount for all related child objects under the Opportunity.
Use the Metadata API to create real-time roll-up summaries.

explanation: Without a master-detail relationship you can't use a roll-up summary field. Instead, you write a trigger on the child object that runs an aggregate query such as SUM() grouped by the Opportunity lookup and updates the parent whenever children are inserted, updated, deleted, or undeleted. A trigger on Opportunity doesn't fire when children change. The Streaming API publishes change notifications, and the Metadata API manages configuration; neither one calculates roll-ups.

text: A developer created a trigger on a custom object that also has dependent picklists. According to Salesforce order of execution, which step happens first?

options.text: The original record is loaded from the database.
System validation is run for maximum field lengths.
Old values are overwritten with the new record values.
JavaScript validation is run in the browser.

explanation: Exam key: On the server, the first step in the save order of execution is loading the original record from the database, or initializing it for an upsert. After that, the old values are overwritten with the new ones and system validation runs, including checks such as maximum field length. Note: Older Salesforce order-of-execution docs said that before any server-side step, the browser runs JavaScript validation when the record has dependent picklist fields, and the stem's mention of dependent picklists points to that answer.
reviewNote: Key may be incorrect: older order-of-execution docs list browser JavaScript validation for dependent picklists before the server steps, which the stem's dependent-picklist hint suggests.

text: Universal Containers implemented a private sharing model for the Account object. A custom Account search tool was developed with Apex to help sales representatives find accounts that match multiple criteria they specify. Since its release, users of the tool report they can see Accounts they do not own. What should the developer use to enforce sharing permissions for the currently logged in user while using the custom search tool?

options.text: Use the with sharing keyword on the class declaration.
Use the without sharing keyword on the class declaration.
Use the userInfo Apex class to filter all SOQL queries to returned records owned by the logged-in user.
Use the schema describe calls to determine if the logged-in user has access to the Account object.

explanation: Declaring the class with sharing makes its SOQL queries respect the running user's sharing rules, so under a private model the search returns only Accounts the user owns or has been granted access to. without sharing explicitly ignores sharing, which would keep the problem. Filtering by UserInfo owner would wrongly hide records shared through rules or the role hierarchy. Schema describe calls check object-level permissions, not record-level access.

text: Universal Containers has a support process that allows users to request support from its engineering team using a custom object, Engineering_Support__c. Users should be able to associate multiple Engineering_Support__c records with one Opportunity. Aggregate information about those records must also appear on the Opportunity. Which relationship field supports these requirements?

options.text: Lookup field from Opportunity to Engineering_Support__c
Master-detail field from Engineering_Support__c to Opportunity
Master-detail field from Opportunity to Engineering_Support__c
Lookup field from Engineering_Support__c to Opportunity

explanation: A master-detail field on Engineering_Support__c pointing to Opportunity makes each Opportunity the parent of many support records and lets you create roll-up summary fields on Opportunity to aggregate them. A lookup from support records to Opportunity also allows many children, but standard roll-up summaries aren't available on lookups. Putting the relationship field on Opportunity would link each Opportunity to only one support record.

text: A developer is creating an app that contains multiple Lightning web components. One of the child components is used for navigation purposes. When a user clicks a button called Next in the child component, the parent component must be alerted so it can navigate to the next page. How should this be accomplished?

options.text: Update a property on the parent.
Call a method in the Apex controller.
Fire a notification.
Create a custom event.

explanation: In LWC, a child talks to its parent by dispatching a custom event, for example this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('next')), which the parent handles with an onnext listener. A child can't set properties on its parent, because data flows down through public properties. Calling Apex doesn't notify the parent component. Firing a notification isn't a component-communication mechanism.

text: Which annotation exposes an Apex class as a RESTful web service?

options.text: @RemoteAction
@RestResource(urlMapping='/myService/*')
@HttpInvocable
@AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)

explanation: @RestResource(urlMapping='/myService/*') on a global class exposes it as a REST endpoint, and its methods are mapped with annotations such as @HttpGet and @HttpPost. @RemoteAction is for Visualforce JavaScript remoting, @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true) exposes methods to Lightning components, and @HttpInvocable isn't a valid annotation.

text: Universal Containers is building a recruiting app with an Applicant object that stores information about an individual person and a Job object that represents a job. Each applicant may apply for more than one job. What should a developer implement to represent that an applicant has applied for a job?

options.text: Junction object between Applicant and Job
Lookup field from Applicant to Job
Master-detail field from Applicant to Job
Formula field on Applicant that references Job

explanation: An applicant can apply for many jobs, and a job can have many applicants, so this is a many-to-many relationship. In Salesforce you model it with a junction object (for example, Application) that has two master-detail fields, one to Applicant and one to Job. A single lookup or master-detail field from Applicant to Job allows only one job per applicant, and a formula field can't create a relationship.

text: A developer is implementing an Apex class for a financial system. Within the class, the variables 'creditAmount' and 'debitAmount' should not be able to change once a value is assigned. In which two ways can the developer declare the variables to ensure their value can only be assigned one time? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Use the static keyword and assign its value in a static initializer.
Use the final keyword and assign its value in the class constructor.
Use the final keyword and assign its value when declaring the variable.
Use the static keyword and assign its value in the class constructor.

explanation: A final variable can be assigned only once: either when it's declared or, for instance variables, in the constructor or an initializer block. After that, any reassignment causes a compile error. The static keyword only makes a variable belong to the class rather than to each instance; it doesn't block reassignment, so the static-initializer and static-in-constructor options don't guarantee the value is set only once.

text: Which scenario is valid for execution by unit tests?

options.text: Execute anonymous Apex as a different user.
Generate a Visualforce PDF with getContentAsPDF().
Load data from a remote site with a callout.
Set the created date of a record using a system method.

explanation: Test.setCreatedDate(recordId, dateTime) sets the CreatedDate of a record inserted in a test, which is a supported way to test date-based logic. Test methods can't make real callouts and must use a mock. getContentAsPDF() isn't supported in test methods. Execute Anonymous isn't part of a unit test; tests use System.runAs to switch the running user.

text: Developers at Universal Containers (UC) use version control to share their code changes, but they notice that when they deploy their code to different environments they often have failures. They decide to set up Continuous Integration (CI). What should the UC development team use to automatically run tests as part of their CI process?

options.text: Salesforce CLI
Visual Studio Code
Force.com Toolkit
Developer Console

explanation: The Salesforce CLI can be scripted, so a CI server can call it to authenticate, deploy, and run Apex tests (for example, sf apex run test) automatically on every commit. Visual Studio Code and the Developer Console are interactive tools that a developer drives by hand. Force.com Toolkit isn't a tool for running tests in a CI pipeline.

text: A developer is asked to prevent anyone other than a user with Sales Manager profile from changing the Opportunity Status to Closed Lost if the lost reason is blank. Which automation allows the developer to satisfy this requirement in the most efficient manner?

options.text: An Apex trigger on Opportunity
An error-condition formula in an Opportunity validation rule
A record-triggered flow on Opportunity
An approval process on Opportunity

explanation: A validation rule can enforce this without code. For example, the error condition is true when the stage is Closed Lost, the Lost Reason is blank, and $Profile.Name isn't Sales Manager, so the save is blocked with a message. An Apex trigger or a record-triggered flow could do the same thing but takes more effort to build and maintain. An approval process routes records for sign-off and doesn't block an edit.

text: A developer created a trigger on the Account object and wants to test if the trigger is properly bulkified. The developer team decided that the trigger should be tested with 200 account records with unique names. What two things should be done to create the test data within the unit test with the least amount of code? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Use @isTest(SeeAllData=true) on the test class.
Use @isTest(isParallel=true) on the test class.
Create a static resource containing test data.
Use Test.loadData() to populate data in the test method.

explanation: You can store the 200 Account rows as a CSV in a static resource and load them with one call, Test.loadData(Account.sObjectType, 'resourceName'), which inserts the records and returns them with almost no code. SeeAllData=true exposes existing org data instead of creating controlled test data. isParallel=true only controls whether tests run in parallel.

text: A business has a proprietary Order Management System (OMS) that creates and fulfills website orders. An integration creates the corresponding Order record in Salesforce and relates it to a Contact identified by email. As the order advances through OMS stages, the integration updates Salesforce, but each update is creating a new Order. Which two actions should prevent duplicate Order records? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Use the order number from the OMS as an external ID.
Ensure that the order number in the OMS is unique.
Use the Contact email address as the Order External ID.
Write an Order trigger that deletes duplicates.

explanation: Each update creates a new Order because the integration has no stable key to match on. If the OMS order number is unique and stored in an External ID field, the integration can upsert on that field, so updates find the existing Order. A Contact email can't serve as the Order key because one contact can place many orders. A trigger that deletes duplicates hides the symptom after the fact and leaves the integration's logic broken.

text: Which three data types can a SOQL query return? Choose 3 answers

options.text: Double
Long
sObject
Integer
List

explanation: Exam key: The listed answers are Double, sObject, and List. The reasoning is that a query returns a list of records, a single record when assigned to an sObject variable, and numeric values from aggregate functions. Note: According to the Apex documentation, a SOQL query returns a List<sObject>, a single sObject, or an Integer for SELECT COUNT(). Aggregate queries return AggregateResult objects rather than a Double, so the documentation-supported answer is sObject, Integer, and List.
reviewNote: Key appears incorrect: Apex docs say SOQL returns List, sObject, or Integer (COUNT()), not Double.

text: A developer created a new after insert trigger on the Lead object that creates Task records for each Lead. After deploying to production, an existing outside integration that inserts Lead records in batches to Salesforce is occasionally reporting total batch failures being caused by the Task insert statement. This causes the integration process in the outside system to stop, requiring a manual restart. Which change should the developer make to allow the integration to continue when some records in a batch cause failures due to the Task insert statement, so that manual restarts are not needed?

options.text: Use a Database DML method with allOrNone set to false.
Deactivate the trigger before the integration runs.
Remove the Apex class from the integration user's profile.
Wrap the Task DML operation in a try/catch block.

explanation: Using Database.insert(tasks, false) with allOrNone set to false allows partial success. Tasks that fail come back as Database.SaveResult errors instead of throwing an exception, so the Lead batch isn't rolled back. A try/catch around a regular insert catches the exception but gives no row-by-row success. Deactivating the trigger or changing profile access would just switch off the required Task creation.

text: Which two statements are true about using the @testSetup annotation in an Apex test class? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Records created in the test setup method cannot be updated in individual test methods.
In a test setup method, test data is inserted once and made available to all test methods in the test class.
A method defined with @testSetup executes once for each test method and counts toward that test method's governor limits.
@testSetup is not supported when @isTest(SeeAllData=true) is used.

explanation: An @testSetup method runs once per test class, and every test method gets a fresh copy of those records. Changes a test method makes are rolled back before the next one runs, so test methods can update the setup records. The setup method isn't re-run for each test method. Test setup methods aren't supported in classes annotated with @isTest(SeeAllData=true).

text: A Salesforce administrator created a flow named accountOnboarding that must run inside an Aura component. Which tag should a developer use to display the flow?

options.text: <lightning:flow aura:id="flowData" />
<lightning:flowData />
<aura:flow />
<force:flow />

explanation: The lightning:flow component embeds a flow in an Aura component. You give it an aura:id, then in the controller you find it and call startFlow('accountOnboarding'). The tags lightning:flowData, aura:flow, and force:flow don't exist.

text: A developer is alerted to an issue with a custom trigger that is causing records to be duplicated. What is the most appropriate debugging approach to troubleshoot the issue?

options.text: Review the Historical Event logs to identify the source of the issue.
Add system.debug statements to the code to track the execution flow and identify the issue.
Use the Apex Interactive Debugger to step through the code and identify the issue.
Disable the trigger in production and test to see if the issue still occurs.

explanation: The Apex Interactive Debugger lets a developer set breakpoints and step through the trigger line by line in a sandbox, inspecting variables to see exactly where duplicates are created. Adding System.debug statements also works but is slower trial and error. Event logs show activity, not the trigger's logic. Disabling the trigger in production disrupts the business and doesn't explain the cause.

text: Managers at Universal Containers want to ensure that only decommissioned containers are able to be deleted in the system. To meet the business requirement a Salesforce developer adds "Decommissioned" as a picklist value for the Status__c custom field within the Container__c object. Which two approaches could a developer use to enforce only Container records with a status of "Decommissioned" can be deleted? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Before-delete record-triggered flow
Before-delete Apex trigger
After-delete record-triggered flow
Validation rule

explanation: A before-delete Apex trigger can call addError() on records whose Status__c isn't Decommissioned to block the deletion. A record-triggered flow set to run when a record is deleted runs before the delete, and its Custom Error element can stop it the same way. An after-delete flow runs only after the record is already gone. Validation rules don't run on delete.

text: A team of developers is working on a source-driven project that allows them to work independently, with many different org configurations. Which type of Salesforce orgs should they use for their development?

options.text: Developer sandboxes.
Full sandboxes
Developer orgs
Scratch orgs

explanation: Scratch orgs are temporary orgs built from source and a definition file, so each developer can spin up an isolated org with whatever features and settings a feature needs, which fits source-driven development. Developer and Full sandboxes are copies of production, so their configuration is tied to it. Developer Edition orgs are long-lived and not set up from source.

text: A company decides to implement a new process where every time an Opportunity is created, a follow up Task should be created and assigned to the Opportunity Owner. What is the most efficient way for a developer to implement this?

options.text: trigger on Task
Task actions
Auto-launched flow on Task
Record-triggered flow on Opportunity

explanation: A record-triggered flow on Opportunity, set to run when a record is created, can create the follow-up Task and assign it to the Opportunity's owner without code. A trigger or an autolaunched flow on Task starts from the wrong object, since the event is the Opportunity being created. Task actions are quick actions a user clicks by hand, not automation.

text: A developer is creating a page that allows users to create multiple Opportunities. The developer is asked to verify the current user's default Opportunity record type, and set certain default values based on the record type before inserting the record. How can the developer find the current user's default record type?

options.text: Create the Opportunity and inspect RecordTypeId before insert, assuming Salesforce has already assigned the user's default record type.
Query the user's Profile and call a getDefaultRecordType() method for Opportunity.
Use a Schema.UserInfo.Opportunity.getDefaultRecordType() method.
Use Opportunity.sObjectType.getDescribe().getRecordTypeInfos() and find the RecordTypeInfo where isDefaultRecordTypeMapping() is true.

explanation: Calling Opportunity.sObjectType.getDescribe().getRecordTypeInfos() returns RecordTypeInfo entries for the running user, and the one whose isDefaultRecordTypeMapping() returns true is the user's default. A new Opportunity in Apex doesn't get its RecordTypeId filled in before insert. There is no getDefaultRecordType() method on Profile, and Schema.UserInfo.Opportunity isn't valid syntax.

text: The Account object has a master-detail child object called Branch__c. The org also has roll-up summary fields, custom validation rules, and duplicate rules. A developer creates a trigger on Account. Which two things should the developer consider while testing the trigger? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Roll-up summary field recalculations can cause a parent record to go through the save process again.
Duplicate rules execute only after all DML operations commit to the database.
The trigger may fire multiple times during a transaction.
Validation rules always cause the trigger to fire again.
