explanation: When a child Branch__c record changes, the roll-up summary on Account recalculates and the Account goes through the save process again, which can fire Account triggers a second time. Workflow field updates and flows can also re-fire triggers within one transaction, so the trigger has to handle repeated runs. Duplicate rules run during the save, before the commit. Validation rules don't cause a trigger to fire again.

text: A PrimaryId__c custom field exists on the Candidate__c object. It stores each candidate's identifier and is marked Unique. Universal Containers has a CSV with updated data keyed by PrimaryId__c and wants each row mapped to the correct Candidate record during upload. Which technique streamlines the upload?

options.text: Upload the CSV into a custom object related to Candidate__c.
Create a before-insert trigger to map the records.
Mark PrimaryId__c as an External ID.
Create a before-save flow to map the records.

explanation: When PrimaryId__c is marked as an External ID, Data Loader or the Data Import Wizard can upsert on that field and match each CSV row to its existing Candidate record, without first looking up Salesforce Ids. Loading the CSV into a related staging object, or writing a trigger or flow to do the mapping, adds custom work that the External ID upsert already handles.

text:
A Developer Edition org has five existing Accounts. The following Execute Anonymous code runs: 
Account myAccount = new Account(Name = 'MyAccount');
insert myAccount;
Integer x = 1;
List<Account> newAccounts = new List<Account>();
do {
    Account acct = new Account(Name = 'New Account ' + x++);
    newAccounts.add(acct);
} while (x < 10);
How many total Accounts are in the org after this code executes?
explanation: The org starts with five Accounts, and the explicit insert myAccount adds a sixth. The do-while loop only builds nine Account objects in the newAccounts list in memory. The list is never inserted, so none of those records are saved. The final total is 6, not 15 or 10.

text: A developer wants to access the standard price book while writing a test class that covers an OpportunityLineItem trigger. Which method provides the standard price book ID?

options.text: Use Test.getStandardPricebookId() to get the standard price book ID.
Use @isTest(SeeAllData=true) and query the standard price book.
Use @TestVisible to expose the standard price book.
Use Test.loadData() and a static resource to create the standard price book.

explanation: Test.getStandardPricebookId() returns the standard price book's Id in a test without SeeAllData, so you can create PricebookEntry records and then OpportunityLineItems. Querying with SeeAllData=true makes the test depend on org data and is discouraged. @TestVisible only exposes private members to tests. You can't create the standard price book with Test.loadData().

text: A developer must create a Lightning component that allows users to input Contact record information to create a Contact record, including a Salary__c custom field. What should the developer use, along with a lightning-record-edit-form, so that Salary__c field functions as a currency input and is only viewable and editable by users that have the correct field-level permissions on Salary__c?

options.text: <lightning-input type="number" value={salary} formatter="currency"></lightning-input>
<lightning-formatted-number value={salary} format-style="currency"></lightning-formatted-number>
<lightning-input-field field-name="Salary__c"></lightning-input-field>
<lightning-input-currency value={salary}></lightning-input-currency>

explanation: Inside a lightning-record-edit-form, <lightning-input-field field-name="Salary__c"> renders the right input for the field type, here a currency input, and respects field-level security, so users without access don't see or edit it. A lightning-input with a number type doesn't enforce FLS. lightning-formatted-number is display-only. lightning-input-currency isn't a base component.

text: If Apex code executes inside the execute() method of an Apex class when implementing the Batchable interface, which two statements are true regarding governor limits? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Apex governor limits are reset for each execution of the execute() method.
Apex governor limits cannot be exceeded because the transaction is asynchronous.
Apex uses the asynchronous governor-limit levels.
Apex governor limits are omitted while the Batchable class constructor runs.

explanation: Each call to a batch class's execute() method is its own transaction, so governor limits reset for every chunk of records. Batch Apex is asynchronous, so it uses the higher asynchronous limits, such as 200 SOQL queries and 12 MB of heap. Limits still apply and can be exceeded. Running the constructor doesn't exempt code from governor limits.

text: A developer must perform a complex SOQL query that joins two objects in a Lightning component. How can the Lightning component execute the query?

options.text: Write the query in a custom Lightning Web Component wrapper and invoke from the Lightning component.
Invoke an Apex class with the method annotated as @AuraEnabled to perform the query.
Use the Salesforce Streaming API to perform the SOQL query.
Create a Flow to execute the query and invoke it from the Lightning component.

explanation: Lightning components can't run SOQL directly, so the component calls a server-side Apex method annotated with @AuraEnabled, which runs the query (including relationship joins) and returns the results. LWC wrappers run on the client and also can't run SOQL. The Streaming API pushes event notifications, and a flow isn't the standard way for a component to run a complex query.

text: Which two operations affect the number of times a trigger can fire? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Criteria-based sharing calculations
Email messages
Roll-up summary fields
After-save record-triggered flow

explanation: Roll-up summary fields and after-save record-triggered flows both trigger further saves. A roll-up recalculation saves the parent record, and an after-save flow that updates records sends them through DML again, so either one can make a trigger fire more than once in a transaction. Criteria-based sharing recalculation and email messages don't run the record save process that fires triggers.

text: Which two are best practices when it comes to Aura component and application event handling? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Try to use application events as opposed to component events.
Reuse the event logic in a component bundle, by putting the logic in the helper.
Use component events to communicate actions that should be handled at the application level.
Handle low-level events in the event handler and re-fire them as higher-level events.

explanation: Aura event best practices recommend putting reusable event logic in the bundle's helper and having handlers catch low-level events, such as a click, then fire a more meaningful, higher-level event. Component events should be used instead of application events whenever possible, because application events broadcast to everything. Component events are meant for parent and ancestor communication, not for actions handled at the application level.

text: What are three considerations when using the @InvocableMethod annotation in Apex? Choose 3 answers.

options.text: Only one method using @InvocableMethod can be defined per Apex class.
A method using @InvocableMethod can have multiple input parameters.
A method using @InvocableMethod must be declared static.
A method using @InvocableMethod must define a return value.
A method using @InvocableMethod can be declared public or global.

explanation: Only one method per Apex class can carry @InvocableMethod. It must be static, and it can be public or global. It takes at most one input parameter (usually a List of a primitive, sObject, or @InvocableVariable wrapper type), and the return value is optional, so it can return void.

text: Which two access settings must be defined to update a junction-object record? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Read/Write access on the secondary relationship
Read/Write access on the primary relationship
Read/Write access on the junction object
Read access on the primary relationship

explanation: A junction object's record access comes from its two master records, so to update a junction record a user needs Read/Write access to the junction object itself plus Read/Write access to the primary master record. Read-only access on the primary master isn't enough to edit. Read/Write on the secondary master isn't one of the two required settings here.

text: A developer wrote Apex code that calls out to an external system using REST API. How should a developer write the test to prove the code is working as intended?

options.text: Write a class that implements HttpCalloutMock.
Write a class that extends WebServiceMock.
Write a class that implements WebServiceMock.
Write a class that extends HttpCalloutMock.

explanation: To test HTTP (REST) callouts, you write a test class that implements the HttpCalloutMock interface and its respond(HttpRequest) method, then register it with Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, new MyMock()). WebServiceMock is for SOAP callouts generated from WSDL. Both mocks are interfaces, so a class implements them rather than extending them.

text: Universal Containers wants to assess the advantages of declarative development versus programmatic customization for specific use cases in its Salesforce implementation. What are two characteristics of declarative development over programmatic customization? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Declarative development does not require Apex test classes.
Declarative development has higher design limits and query limits
Declarative development can be done using the Setup menu.
Declarative code logic does not require maintenance or review.

explanation: Declarative tools such as flows and validation rules are configured in Setup with point-and-click tools and don't require Apex test classes or code coverage. Declarative automation still runs under the same governor limits as Apex, so it doesn't get higher query limits. It also still needs maintenance, testing, and review as requirements change.

text: How is a controller and extension specified for a custom object named "Notice" on a Visualforce page?

options.text: <apex:page standardController="Notice__c" extensions="myControllerExtension">
<apex:page controllers="Notice__c, myControllerExtension">
<apex:page="Notice__c" extends="myControllerExtension">
<apex:page controller="Notice__c" extensions="myControllerExtension">

explanation: A controller extension adds to a standard controller, so the page names the custom object's API name in standardController="Notice__c" and the extension class in extensions="myControllerExtension". controller= expects a custom Apex controller class, not an object name. controllers and extends aren't valid apex:page attributes.

text: Universal Containers wants a list button to display a Visualforce page that allows users to edit multiple records. Which Visualforce feature supports this requirement?

options.text: Standard Controller with Custom List Controller extension
Custom list controller with recordSetVar page attribute
Controller extension and <apex:listButton> tag
Standard controller and the recordSetVar page attribute

explanation: A list button can open a Visualforce page that uses a standard controller together with the recordSetVar attribute. This turns on the standard list (set) controller, so the page receives the selected or filtered records and can edit and save them together. The other combinations either aren't how list buttons get their records, or apex:listButton isn't a real tag.

text: A team of many developers work in their own individual orgs that have the same configuration as the production org. Which type of org is best suited for this scenario?

options.text: Developer Sandbox
Full Sandbox
Developer Edition
Partner Developer Edition

explanation: A Developer sandbox copies production's metadata (configuration and code but not data), so each developer can work in an isolated org that matches production. A Full sandbox is expensive, copies all data, and is meant for staging and performance testing. Developer Edition and Partner Developer Edition orgs are standalone and don't copy production's configuration.

text: Which code statement includes an Apex method named updateAccounts in the class AccountController for use in a Lightning Web Component?

options.text: import updateAccounts from 'AccountController';
import updateAccounts from '@salesforce/apex/AccountController';
import updateAccounts from 'AccountController.updateAccounts';
import updateAccounts from '@salesforce/apex/AccountController.updateAccounts';

explanation: Apex methods are imported into LWC from the @salesforce/apex module, using the format @salesforce/apex/ClassName.methodName. For this method that is import updateAccounts from '@salesforce/apex/AccountController.updateAccounts';. The other options are missing the @salesforce/apex namespace or the method name, so they don't resolve.

text: For which three items can a trace flag be configured? Choose 3 answers

options.text: Apex Class
Flow
User
Visualforce
Trigger

explanation: In Setup, trace flags can be set on a user, an Apex class, or an Apex trigger, which controls debug log levels for that entity's activity. Flows and Visualforce pages aren't entity types you can set a trace flag on. Their activity shows up in a user's debug logs instead.

text: Which exception type cannot be caught?

options.text: Custom exception
LimitException
NoAccessException
CalloutException

explanation: System.LimitException is thrown when a governor limit is exceeded and cannot be caught; the transaction is terminated and any catch block is skipped. Custom exceptions, NoAccessException, and CalloutException are ordinary catchable exceptions that can be handled in a try/catch block. To protect against limits, code should check the Limits class proactively rather than rely on catching the failure.

text: What should a developer do to check the code coverage of a class after running all tests?

options.text: View the code coverage percentage for the class using the Overall Code Coverage panel in the Developer Console Tests tab.
View the Class Test Percentage tab on the Apex Class list view in Salesforce Setup.
Select and run the class on the Apex Test Execution page in the Developer Console.
View the Code Coverage column in the Apex Classes list view in Setup.

explanation: After a test run, the Developer Console Tests tab shows the Overall Code Coverage panel, which lists each class and trigger with its coverage percentage, and double-clicking a class highlights covered and uncovered lines. There is no Class Test Percentage tab, and the Apex Classes list in Setup does not provide a per-class coverage column for this purpose. Running a single class on the test execution page would only produce coverage from that run, not after running all tests.

text: What are three capabilities of the <ltng: require> tag when loading JavaScript resources in Aura components? Choose 3 answers

options.text: One-time loading for duplicate scripts
Loading scripts in parallel
Loading Files from Documents
Specifying loading order
Loading externally hosted scripts

explanation: <ltng:require> loads JavaScript and CSS from static resources, and it loads a duplicate resource only once even when several components request it. Scripts within one tag load in the order they are listed, while separate <ltng:require> tags let independent sets of scripts load in parallel. It cannot load files from Documents, and externally hosted scripts are blocked by Lightning Locker and Content Security Policy, so libraries must be uploaded as static resources.

text: A custom picklist field Pool_Preference__c contains the values 'Vegan', 'Kosher', and 'No Preference'. The developer must ensure users always select a value. Which configuration enforces the requirement at the field level?

options.text: Set "Use the first value in the list as the default value" to True.
Write an Apex trigger to ensure a value is selected.
Mark the field as Required on the object page layout.
Mark the field as Required on the field definition.

explanation: Marking the field as Required on the field definition makes it universally required, so every save through the UI, API, Data Loader, or Apex must include a value. Required on a page layout only applies to that layout in the UI and is bypassed by API loads. A default value pre-fills the field but users can still clear it. A trigger works but is unnecessary code when a declarative field-level setting exists.

text: A developer is reviewing a ContactSearch Apex method that builds dynamic SOQL by concatenating the lastName parameter into a WHERE clause. Which two techniques can prevent SOQL injection? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Use variable binding and replace the dynamic query with static SOQL.
Use String.escapeSingleQuotes() to sanitize the parameter before using it in dynamic SOQL.
Use the @ReadOnly annotation and with sharing on the class.
Use a regular expression to remove special characters from the parameter.

explanation: Replacing the concatenated query with static SOQL and a bind variable such as WHERE LastName = :lastName treats the input strictly as data, which removes the injection risk. If dynamic SOQL must stay, String.escapeSingleQuotes() escapes quotes in the input so it cannot break out of the string literal. @ReadOnly and with sharing control query limits and record access, not injection. A hand-written regex is error-prone and can strip legitimate characters, so it is not a recommended technique.

text: What are two benefits of using External IDs? Choose 2 answers

options.text: An External ID field can be used to reference an ID from another external system.
An External ID can be a formula field to create a unique key from two Salesforce fields.
An External ID can be used with Salesforce Mobile to make external data visible.
An External ID is indexed and can improve SOQL query performance.

explanation: An External ID stores a record's identifier from another system, enabling matching and upsert operations during integrations and imports. External ID fields are also automatically indexed, so filtering on them in SOQL performs better. Formula fields cannot be marked as External IDs, and an External ID does not make external data visible in Salesforce Mobile; that is the job of Salesforce Connect external objects.

text: What are two characteristics related to formulas? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Formulas are calculated at runtime and are not stored in the database.
Formulas can reference themselves.
Formulas can reference values in related objects.
Fields that are used in a formula field can be deleted or edited without editing the formula.

explanation: Formula fields are read-only values calculated when the record is read; they are not stored in the database. Formulas can also use cross-object references to pull values from related parent records, such as Account.Industry on a Contact. A formula cannot reference itself, since that would be circular, and a field referenced by a formula cannot be deleted until the formula is changed to remove the reference.

text:
What is the result of this Apex code? 
Account a = new Account();
Database.insert(a, false);

options.text: The record is not created and an exception is thrown.
The record is not created and no exception is thrown.
The record is created and no error is reported.
The record is created and a message is written to the debug log.

explanation: Account Name is required, so this insert fails validation. With allOrNone set to false, Database.insert(a, false) does not throw a DmlException for record-level errors; it returns a Database.SaveResult whose isSuccess() is false and whose getErrors() contains the failure. Because the snippet never checks the result, the record is silently not created. A plain insert a statement would have thrown an exception instead.

text: A developer has a single custom controller class that works with a Visualforce Wizard to support creating and editing multiple sObjects. The wizard accepts data from user inputs across multiple Visualforce pages and from a parameter on the initial URL. Which three statements are useful inside the unit test to effectively test the custom controller? Choose 3 answers

options.text: String nextPage = controller.save().getUrl();
ApexPages.currentPage().getParameters().put('input', 'TestValue');
insert pageRef;
public ExtendedController(ApexPages.StandardController controller) { }
Test.setCurrentPage(pageRef);

explanation: A Visualforce controller test should set the page context with Test.setCurrentPage(pageRef), simulate the URL parameter with ApexPages.currentPage().getParameters().put('input', 'TestValue'), and call controller actions such as save(), checking the returned PageReference URL to verify navigation through the wizard. A PageReference is not an sObject, so insert pageRef is invalid. A constructor declaration belongs in the controller or extension class itself, not in a test method.

text: A developer is designing a new application on the Salesforce platform and wants to ensure it can support multiple tenants effectively. Which design framework should the developer consider to ensure scalability and maintainability?

options.text: Waterfall Model
Flux (view, action, dispatcher, and store)
Model-View-Controller (MVC)
Agile Development

explanation: Salesforce follows the Model-View-Controller pattern: sObjects and the database form the model, Visualforce pages and Lightning components form the view, and Apex controllers and JavaScript controllers form the controller. Separating these layers keeps multi-tenant applications maintainable and scalable. Waterfall and Agile are project-management methodologies rather than application design frameworks, and Flux is a front-end data-flow pattern that is not the platform's architectural model.

text: A developer at AW Computing must create a test class for customization that uses Pricing_Structure__c records. The pricing structure contains more than 500 records. Which two approaches can the developer use to ensure Pricing_Structure__c test records are available when the test class executes? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Use a Test Data Factory class.
Use the @isTest(SeeAllData=true) annotation.
Use Test.loadData() with a CSV static resource.
Use without sharing on the class declaration.

explanation: A test data factory class can generate all the needed Pricing_Structure__c records in code, and Test.loadData() can load a predefined CSV static resource in a single call, which suits a set of more than 500 records. Both approaches create data inside the test context, so tests stay isolated from org data. @isTest(SeeAllData=true) makes tests depend on existing org data and is discouraged. without sharing affects record access, not whether test data exists.

text:
Given the Apex statement: 
Account myAccount = [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account];
What occurs when the SOQL query returns more than one Account?

options.text: The variable, myaccount, is automatically cast to the List data type.
An unhandled exception is thrown and the code terminates.
The query fails and an error is written to the debug log.
The first Account returned is assigned to myAccount.

explanation: Assigning a SOQL query directly to a single sObject variable requires exactly one row. If the query returns more than one Account, or none, Apex throws a System.QueryException ("List has more than 1 row for assignment to SObject"), and unless it is caught, execution stops. Apex does not automatically turn the variable into a List, does not quietly pick the first record, and does not just log an error and continue.

text: What should a developer use to fix a Lightning Web Component bug in a sandbox?

options.text: Developer Console
Force.com IDE
Execute Anonymous
VS Code

explanation: Lightning Web Components are developed and fixed in VS Code with the Salesforce Extension Pack and Salesforce CLI, which retrieve the component bundle from the sandbox, let you edit and debug it, and deploy it back. The Developer Console cannot create or edit LWC bundles, and Execute Anonymous only runs Apex. The Force.com IDE (Eclipse) has been retired and never supported LWC.

text: A developer must write an Apex method that will be called from a Lightning component. The method may delete an Account stored in the accountRec variable. Which method should a developer use to ensure only users that should be able to delete Accounts can successfully perform deletions?

options.text: accountRec.isDeletable()
Schema.sObjectType.Account.isDeletable()
accountRec.sObjectType.isDeletable()
Account.isDeletable()

explanation: Schema.sObjectType.Account.isDeletable() uses the DescribeSObjectResult for Account to check whether the running user has object-level permission to delete Accounts, so the Apex method can enforce CRUD before running delete accountRec. There is no isDeletable() method on an sObject record instance or directly on the Account type, and accountRec.sObjectType is not valid syntax for a record variable, so the other forms do not compile.

text:
A lead developer creates an Apex interface called Laptop. Consider the following code snippet: 
public class SilverLaptop {
    // code implementation
}
How can a developer use the Laptop interface within the SilverLaptop class?

options.text: Extends (class="Laptop") public class SilverLaptop
public class SilverLaptop implements Laptop
public class SilverLaptop extends Laptop
Interface (class="Laptop") public class SilverLaptop

explanation: In Apex, a class uses an interface with the implements keyword, as in public class SilverLaptop implements Laptop, and must then provide concrete implementations of all the interface's methods. extends is for inheriting from a virtual or abstract class, not an interface. The Extends (class="Laptop") and Interface (class="Laptop") forms are made-up annotation-style syntax that Apex does not support.

text: What should a developer use to obtain the Id and Name of all Leads, Accounts, and Contacts that match the name "Universal Containers"?

options.text: FIND 'Universal Containers' IN COMPANY NAME FIELDS RETURNING Lead(Id, Name), Account(Id, Name), Contact(Id, Name)
SELECT Lead.Id, Lead.Name, Account.Id, Account.Name, Contact.Id, Contact.Name FROM Lead, Account, Contact WHERE Name = 'Universal Containers'
FIND 'Universal Containers' IN NAME FIELDS RETURNING Lead(Id, Name), Account(Id, Name), Contact(Id, Name)
SELECT Lead(Id, Name), Account(Id, Name), Contact(Id, Name) FROM Lead, Account, Contact WHERE Name = 'Universal Containers'

explanation: SOSL is the right tool for searching several objects in one call. FIND 'Universal Containers' IN NAME FIELDS RETURNING Lead(Id, Name), Account(Id, Name), Contact(Id, Name) searches name fields and returns matching Leads, Accounts, and Contacts together. COMPANY NAME FIELDS is not a valid SOSL search group; valid groups are ALL, NAME, EMAIL, PHONE, and SIDEBAR FIELDS. SOQL cannot query several unrelated objects in a single FROM clause, so both SELECT options are invalid.

text: A credit card company needs to implement the functionality for a service agent to process damaged or stolen credit cards. When the customers call in, the service agent must gather many pieces of information. A developer is tasked to implement this functionality. What should the developer use to satisfy this requirement in the most efficient manner?

options.text: Screen-based flow
Approval process
trigger
Lightning Component

explanation: A screen flow guides the agent through a series of screens to capture many inputs, with branching logic and record updates, all built declaratively and without code, which makes it the most efficient choice. An approval process routes records for sign-off and does not collect data interactively. A trigger runs on DML with no user interface. A custom Lightning component could work, but it requires much more development effort.

text: A custom Visualforce controller calls the ApexPages.addMessage() method, but no messages are rendering on the page. Which component should be added to the Visualforce page to display the message?

options.text: <apex:message for="info"/>
<apex:pageMessages />
<apex:pageMessage severity="info" />
<apex:facet name="messages" />

explanation: <apex:pageMessages /> displays every message in the page's message collection, including those added in the controller with ApexPages.addMessage(), so adding it makes the messages appear. <apex:message for="..."/> shows only the message for one specific component. <apex:pageMessage> renders a single custom message defined in its own attributes rather than the queued messages. <apex:facet> defines a named region of a parent component and does not display messages.

text: Since Aura application events follow the traditional publish-subscribe model, which method is used to fire an event?

options.text: fire()
sendEvent()
FireEvent()
emit()

explanation: In Aura, you get an application event with $A.get("e.namespace:eventName"), set its parameters with setParams(), and publish it with fire(); every handler registered for that event receives it. sendEvent() and FireEvent() are not Aura methods. emit() belongs to other frameworks, not to the Aura event API.

text:
A developer considers the following Apex code: 
Boolean isOK;
Integer x;
String theString = 'Hello';
if (isOK == false && theString == 'Hello') {
    x = 1;
} else if (isOK == true && theString == 'Hello') {
    x = 2;
} else if (isOK == null && theString == 'Hello') {
    x = 3;
} else {
    x = 4;
}
What is the value of x?
explanation: isOK is declared but never assigned, so its value is null; uninitialized Apex variables, including Booleans, default to null rather than false. The first two conditions fail because null == false and null == true both evaluate to false. The third condition, isOK == null && theString == 'Hello', is true, so x is set to 3 and the final else is never reached.

text: Universal Containers wants to automatically assign new cases to the appropriate support representative based on the case origin. They have created a custom field on the Case object to store the support representative name. What is the best solution to assign the case to the appropriate support representative?

options.text: Use a trigger on the Case object.
Use a formula field on the Case object.
Use a validation rule on the Case object.
Use an Assignment Flow element.

explanation: A record-triggered flow on Case can evaluate the Origin value and use an Assignment element to set the owner or representative field, then save the record, all declaratively. This is the best low-maintenance choice over writing a trigger. A formula field cannot change record ownership or assign work. A validation rule only blocks saves that fail a condition and never assigns anything.

text: When importing and exporting data into Salesforce, which two statements are true? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Bulk API can be used to bypass the storage limits when importing large data volumes in development environments.
Data Import Wizard is an application installed on your computer.
Bulk API can import large data volumes in development environments without bypassing storage limits.
Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes have different storage limits.

explanation: The Bulk API is designed for loading large data volumes, but every record it loads still counts against the org's data storage, so it cannot bypass storage limits in any environment. Sandbox types also have different storage limits: Developer sandboxes allow 200 MB and Developer Pro sandboxes allow 1 GB. The Data Import Wizard runs in the browser from Setup and is not installed locally, unlike Data Loader.

text:
A developer must implement a CheckPaymentProcessor class that provides check processing payment capabilities that adhere to what is defined for payments in the PaymentProcessor interface. 
public interface PaymentProcessor {
    void pay(Decimal amount);
}
Which is the correct implementation to use the PaymentProcessor interface class?

options.text: public class CheckPaymentProcessor implements PaymentProcessor { public void pay(Decimal amount) {} }
public class CheckPaymentProcessor implements PaymentProcessor { public void pay(Decimal amount); }
public class CheckPaymentProcessor extends PaymentProcessor { public void pay(Decimal amount); }
public class CheckPaymentProcessor extends PaymentProcessor { public void pay(Decimal amount) {} }

explanation: A class adopts an interface with implements and must supply a concrete, bodied version of each interface method, so public class CheckPaymentProcessor implements PaymentProcessor { public void pay(Decimal amount) {} } is correct. Declaring pay(Decimal amount); without a body is only valid in an interface or as an abstract method, so it fails to compile in a normal class. extends is used to inherit from classes, not interfaces.

text: Universal Containers decides to use exclusively declarative development to build out a new Salesforce application. Which three options should be used to build out the database layer for the application? Choose 3 answers

options.text: Custom objects and fields
Triggers
Roll-up summaries
Relationships
Flows

explanation: The data model, or database layer, is built declaratively from custom objects and fields, relationships (lookup and master-detail) that connect them, and roll-up summary fields that aggregate child data onto parents. Triggers are code, so they are not purely declarative development. Flows are declarative, but they belong to the business logic and automation layer, not the database layer.

text: The sales management team at Universal Containers requires that the Lead Source field of the Lead record be populated when a Lead is converted What should be done to ensure that a user populates the Lead Source field prior to converting a Lead?

options.text: Create an after trigger on Lead.
Use Lead Conversion field mapping.
Use a formula field.
Use a validation rule.

explanation: A validation rule such as ISPICKVAL(LeadSource, "") combined with a conversion check (for example IsConverted, with validation on lead convert enabled) blocks the save or conversion until the user fills in Lead Source. Lead conversion field mapping only copies Lead values to the resulting Account, Contact, and Opportunity, and cannot force a value to be entered. An after trigger runs too late to prompt the user naturally, and a formula field is read-only, so users cannot populate it.

text: A developer has identified a method in an Apex class that performs resource-intensive actions in memory by iterating over a SOQL result set and also performs DML to save changes. Which two techniques should the developer implement as best practices to monitor governor limits and provide transaction control? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Use the @ReadOnly annotation to bypass the number of rows returned by a SOQL.
Use partial DML statements to ensure only valid data is committed.
Use the Limits class to monitor current governor-limit consumption.
Use Database.setSavepoint() / Database.rollback() for transaction control.

explanation: The Limits class methods, such as Limits.getQueries(), Limits.getCpuTime(), and Limits.getDmlRows(), let the code check how much of each governor limit it has used while processing. Database.setSavepoint() and Database.rollback() give explicit transaction control, so partial changes can be undone if later processing fails. @ReadOnly applies only to specific contexts such as Visualforce and web services, and it forbids DML. Partial-success DML handles row errors but does not monitor limits.

text: Universal Containers has a large number of custom applications that were built using a third-party JavaScript framework and exposed using Visualforce pages. The company wants to update these applications to apply styling that resembles the look and feel of Lightning Experience. What should the developer do to fulfill the business request in the quickest and most effective manner?

options.text: Rewrite all Visualforce pages as Lightning components.
Set the attribute enableLightning to true in the definition.
Enable Available for Lightning Experience, Lightning Communities, and the mobile app on Visualforce pages used by the custom application.
Incorporate the Salesforce Lightning Design System CSS stylesheet Into the JavaScript applications.

explanation: Adding the Salesforce Lightning Design System CSS to the existing pages and JavaScript apps, for example with <apex:slds /> or an SLDS static resource and SLDS class names, gives them a Lightning look without rebuilding them. Rewriting everything as Lightning components would take far longer. There is no enableLightning attribute, and the Available for Lightning Experience checkbox only lets a page run in Lightning; it does not restyle the page.

text: The values 'High', 'Medium', and 'Low' are identified as common values for multiple picklists across different objects. What is an approach a developer can take to streamline maintenance of the picklists and their values, while also restricting the values to the ones mentioned above?

options.text: Create the picklist on each object and use a Global Picklist Value Set containing High, Medium, and Low.
Create the Picklist on each object as a required field and select "Display values alphabetically, not in the order entered".
Create the Picklist on each object and add a validation rule to ensure data integrity.
Create the Picklist on each object and select "Restrict picklist to the values defined in the value set".

explanation: A Global Picklist Value Set defines High, Medium, and Low once and shares them across every picklist field that uses it, so a single change updates all of them. Global value sets are always restricted, so users and the API cannot add other values. Restricting each object's picklist separately still means maintaining each list on its own. Validation rules add upkeep, and sorting values alphabetically only changes display order.

text: Universal Containers is developing a new Lightning Web Component for its marketing department. Which three benefits are associated with the Lightning Component framework? Choose 3 answers

options.text: Better performance due to client-side rendering
Automatic support for accessibility standards
Compatibility with all web browsers
Easy integration with third-party libraries

explanation: Lightning components render on the client, which reduces server round-trips and improves performance. The base components are built to meet accessibility standards out of the box, and the framework supports adding third-party JavaScript libraries loaded as static resources. Compatibility with all web browsers is not guaranteed: Lightning Experience supports only specific desktop and mobile browsers, and older browsers such as Internet Explorer 11 are no longer supported.

text: The OrderHelper utility class contains business logic for processing orders. A developer needs a constant named DELIVERY_MULTIPLIER with a value of 4.15 that must never change after initialization. How should the constant be declared?

options.text: static decimal DELIVERY_MULTIPLIER = 4.15;
constant decimal DELIVERY_MULTIPLIER = 4.15;
static final Decimal DELIVERY_MULTIPLIER = 4.15;
decimal DELIVERY_MULTIPLIER = 4.15;

explanation: In Apex, a constant is declared with static final, as in static final Decimal DELIVERY_MULTIPLIER = 4.15;. final means the value can be assigned only once, and static means one copy is shared at class level, which is the standard pattern for constants. Leaving out final allows the value to be changed later. constant is not an Apex keyword, so that declaration does not compile.

text:
Consider the following code snippet: 
public static List<Lead> obtainAllFields(Set<Id> leadIds) {
    List<Lead> result = new List<Lead>();
    for (Id leadId : leadIds) {
        result.add([SELECT FIELDS(ALL) FROM Lead WHERE Id = :leadId]);
    }
    return result;
}
Given the multi-tenant architecture of the Salesforce platform, what is a best practice a developer should implement to ensure successful execution of the method?

options.text: Avoid using variables as query filters.
Avoid performing queries inside for loops.
Avoid executing queries without a limit clause.
Avoid returning an empty List of records.

explanation: Because the method runs a SOQL query on every pass through the for loop, passing more than 100 Ids exceeds the 100-query synchronous limit and throws a LimitException. Platform best practice is to bulkify the code with one query outside the loop, such as [SELECT FIELDS(ALL) FROM Lead WHERE Id IN :leadIds LIMIT 200]. Bind variables are fine and help prevent injection, and returning an empty list is not a problem. FIELDS(ALL) does require a LIMIT of at most 200, but the main problem here is the query inside the loop.

text: A developer wants to mark each Account in a List<Account> as Active or Inactive based on whether its LastModifiedDate is more than 90 days in the past. Which Apex technique should the developer use?

options.text: An if-else statement, with a for loop inside
A switch statement, with a for loop inside
A for loop, with an if or if/else statement inside
A for loop, with a switch statement inside

explanation: The developer needs to look at each Account, so the outer structure must be a for loop over the list. Inside it, a simple if/else compares LastModifiedDate with a date 90 days ago and sets the status to Active or Inactive. A switch statement matches discrete values and cannot easily test a date range, and putting the loop inside a conditional does not evaluate each record separately.

text: Which three steps allow a custom Scalable Vector Graphic (SVG) to be included in a Lightning web component? Choose 3 answers

options.text: Import the static resource and provide a JavaScript property for it.
Upload the SVG as a static resource.
Reference the import in the HTML template.
Import the SVG as a content asset file.
Reference the property in the HTML template.

explanation: To use a custom SVG in a Lightning web component, upload it as a static resource and import it in JavaScript with import myIcon from '@salesforce/resourceUrl/myIcon';. Then assign the import to a component property and reference that property in the template, for example <img src={iconUrl}>. Templates can only bind to component properties, so they cannot reference the import directly. Content asset files are not the standard route for bundling an SVG resource.

text: What should be used to create scratch orgs?

options.text: Salesforce CLI
Sandbox refresh
Developer Console
Workbench

explanation: Scratch orgs are temporary, source-driven orgs created from a Dev Hub with Salesforce CLI, using sf org create scratch (formerly sfdx force:org:create) and a scratch org definition file. Sandbox refresh copies or recreates sandboxes, not scratch orgs. Neither the Developer Console nor Workbench can create scratch orgs.

text: Universal Containers (UC) uses a custom object called Vendor. The Vendor custom object has a master-detail relationship with the standard Account object. Based on some internal discussions, the UC administrator tried to change the master-detail relationship to a lookup relationship, but was not able to do so. What is a possible reason that this change was not permitted?

options.text: Some of the Vendor records have null for the Account field.
The Account object has a roll-up summary field that summarizes Vendor records.
The Account object does not allow changing a field type for a custom field.
The organization wide default for the Vendor object is Public Read/Write.

explanation: A master-detail relationship cannot be converted to a lookup while the master object has roll-up summary fields that summarize the detail object, so a roll-up on Account over Vendor records blocks the change. Null Account values cannot exist in a master-detail field and would only block conversion in the other direction. Custom relationship fields can change type, and the Vendor object's org-wide default does not stop this conversion.

text: Which three code lines are required to create a Lightning component on a Visualforce page? Choose 3 answers.

options.text: $Lightning.use
$Lightning.useComponent
<apex:includeLightning/>
<apex:slds/>
$Lightning.createComponent

explanation: To embed a Lightning component in a Visualforce page, add <apex:includeLightning/> to load Lightning Components for Visualforce. Then call $Lightning.use() with a Lightning dependency app, and inside its callback call $Lightning.createComponent() to create the component in a DOM element. $Lightning.useComponent does not exist, and <apex:slds/> only adds SLDS styling, so it is not required.

text: Universal Containers is developing a process that requires sales reps to follow scripted steps for each new customer. In the first step, Salesforce must call an ERP REST endpoint to determine whether the customer exists and, if so, present the returned data to the sales rep. Which two components should a developer implement? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Flow
Invocable method
Future method
Trigger

explanation: A screen flow provides the scripted, step-by-step experience for the sales rep and can display the ERP data on a screen. An Apex method marked @InvocableMethod performs the synchronous REST callout and returns the results to the flow as an Apex action. A future method runs asynchronously and cannot return data to the waiting user. A trigger runs on record DML and does not drive a guided user process.

text: What is a benefit of developing applications on a platform-as-a-service environment such as the Salesforce Platform?

options.text: Enforced unit testing and code coverage best practices
Access to predefined computing resources
Preconfigured storage for big data
Unlimited processing power and memory

explanation: With platform as a service, Salesforce provisions, scales, and maintains the servers, storage, and runtime, so developers get predefined, managed computing resources and can focus on building applications. Resources are shared in a multi-tenant system and governed by limits, so processing power and memory are not unlimited. Preconfigured big-data storage is not an inherent PaaS benefit. The 75% coverage rule is a deployment requirement, not a benefit of PaaS itself.

text: Management wants Opportunities to be created automatically for Accounts whose AnnualRevenue exceeds $1,000,000. The current Account trigger runs a SOQL query and inserts an Opportunity inside a loop over Trigger.new. It works for single-record UI updates but fails when 179 Accounts are loaded with Data Loader. Which two changes should the developer make? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Query existing Opportunities outside the for loop.
Check whether all required Opportunity fields are populated before creation.
Collect new Opportunities and perform the insert outside the for loop.
Use Database.query() instead of inline SOQL.

explanation: The trigger fails in bulk because a SOQL query and an insert run for every record, which exceeds the 100-query and 150-DML-statement limits once 179 Accounts are processed. Bulkifying fixes it: query existing Opportunities once outside the loop (for example into a map), add new Opportunities to a list inside the loop, and run one insert afterward. Checking required fields does not address limits, and Database.query() uses the same SOQL limits as inline SOQL.

text: Which action causes a before trigger to fire by default for Accounts?

options.text: Renaming or replacing picklists
Updating addresses using a mass address update tool
Importing data using Data Loader and Bulk API
Converting Leads to Contacts

explanation: Importing records with Data Loader, including through the Bulk API, performs real insert, update, or upsert DML, so before and after triggers on Account fire. Salesforce documents certain operations that do not invoke triggers, including renaming or replacing picklist values and mass address updates. Lead conversion only runs triggers when Require Validation for Converted Leads is enabled, so it does not fire Account triggers by default.

text: Which Apex class contains methods to return the amount of resources that have been used for a particular governor, such as the number of DML statements?

options.text: OrgLimits
Limits
Messaging
Exception

explanation: The Limits class reports governor usage for the current transaction, for example Limits.getDmlStatements() versus Limits.getLimitDmlStatements(), along with methods for queries, CPU time, and heap size. OrgLimits reports org-wide limits such as daily API requests, not per-transaction governor consumption. Messaging sends email, and Exception is the base class for Apex exceptions.

text: A developer is importing sensitive data from an external system into Salesforce. The sensitive fields should not be visible to all users. What should the developer do to enforce access after import?

options.text: Use a third-party tool to encrypt the sensitive data before importing it into Salesforce.
Use Data Loader to import the data and write Apex code to handle security and access control.
Use Data Import Wizard to import the data and configure field-level security to restrict access to sensitive fields.
Use Salesforce CLI to import the data and configure user permissions to restrict access to sensitive data.

explanation: Field-level security is the built-in way to control which profiles and permission sets can see or edit specific fields, so configuring it on the sensitive fields restricts access no matter how the data was loaded. The Data Import Wizard works for loading the records. Encrypting the data externally makes it unusable in Salesforce and does not control visibility. Writing custom Apex for access control duplicates platform security. General user permissions do not control access to individual fields.

text: A developer needs to confirm that a Contact trigger works correctly without changing the organization's data. What should the developer do to test the Contact trigger?

options.text: Deploy an Apex class from VS Code that inserts a Contact.
Create a Contact manually from the Contacts tab.
Use the Test menu in Developer Console to run the test classes for the Contact trigger.
Use Execute Anonymous in Developer Console to insert a Contact.

explanation: Running the trigger's test classes from the Developer Console Test menu runs the test methods in an isolated context where any data they create is rolled back, so the org's real records are never changed. Inserting a Contact with Execute Anonymous, through the UI, or with a class deployed from VS Code all perform real DML and leave data behind. Deploying a class also does not, by itself, insert any record.

text: A developer is integrating with a legacy on-premise SQL database. What should the developer use to ensure the data being integrated is matched to the right records in Salesforce?

options.text: External Object
External ID field
Formula field
Lookup field

explanation: An External ID field on the Salesforce object stores the legacy database's primary key, so imports and integrations can upsert on that key and match each incoming row to the correct existing record. An external object only shows external data in place and does not match it to standard records. Formula fields cannot serve as a matching key. A lookup field links two Salesforce records but cannot identify which record an external row belongs to.

text: Which two requirements must be satisfied when deploying Apex to a production org? Choose 2 answers

options.text: All custom objects must have visibility set to a value other than in Development.
All Apex code must have at least 75% test coverage.
Every Apex trigger must have some test coverage.
All Visual Flows must have at least 1% test coverage.

explanation: To deploy to production, the org's Apex code must have at least 75% overall test coverage, and every trigger must have at least some coverage, more than 0%. All tests must also pass. Custom object deployment status is not part of Apex deployment validation, and there is no rule that flows need 1% coverage. Flow test coverage only applies when an org opts in to require it for deploying active processes and flows.

text: A developer is building a custom Lightning Web Component to collect Contact information. The form is shared by several user groups, and only certain fields should be visible or editable for each user. What should the developer use to respect Salesforce field-level security?

options.text: lightning-input-field
force:inputField
aura:input
ui:inputField

explanation: lightning-input-field, used inside lightning-record-edit-form, is built on Lightning Data Service and automatically respects field-level security. Fields the user cannot see are not shown, and read-only fields cannot be edited. force:inputField and ui:inputField are legacy Aura or Visualforce-era components, and ui components are deprecated. aura:input does not exist, and none of these can be used in a Lightning Web Component.

text: A developer wants to improve runtime performance of Apex calls by caching results on the client. What is the most efficient way to implement this and follow best practices?

options.text: Decorate the server-side method with @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true).
Call the setStorable() method on the action in the JavaScript client-side code.
Decorate the server-side method with @AuraEnabled(storable=true).
Set a cookie in the browser for use upon return to the page.

explanation: Annotating the Apex method with @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true) lets Lightning Data Service cache the response on the client, so repeated calls with the same parameters are served from cache. This is required for @wire and is the recommended approach for both LWC and Aura. setStorable() is the older Aura-only way to mark an action as storable. storable=true is not a valid annotation parameter, and cookies are not a suitable data cache.

text: When a user edits the Postal Code on an Account, a custom Account text field named "Timezone" must be updated based on the values in another custom object called PostalCodeToTimezone__c. What is the optimal way to implement this feature?

options.text: Build a flow with Flow Builder.
Create an account approval process.
Create a formula field.
Build an account assignment rule.

explanation: A record-triggered flow on Account can run when the Postal Code changes, use a Get Records element to look up the matching PostalCodeToTimezone__c record, and update the Timezone field, all declaratively. A formula field cannot query an unrelated custom object that has no relationship to Account. Approval processes route records for sign-off, and assignment rules apply only to Leads and Cases, not Accounts.

text: Universal Containers wants Opportunities to no longer be editable when reaching the Closed/Won stage. How should a developer accomplish this?

options.text: Use a validation rule.
Make fields as read-only on the page layout.
Use the Process Automation settings.
Use Flow Builder.

explanation: A validation rule such as AND(ISPICKVAL(PRIORVALUE(StageName), "Closed Won"), NOT(ISNEW())) blocks saves on Opportunities that were already Closed Won, so the record cannot be edited through any channel. Read-only page layout fields affect only that layout in the UI and are bypassed by the API, inline edits on other layouts, and users with different layouts. Process Automation settings do not lock records, and a flow is a more complex, less direct way to block edits.
